FAITH Foundation
Texas Community Development Block Grant – Housing
Program Narrative

SECTION I: ORGANIZATIONAL OVERVIEW

Legal Name: FAITH Foundation (Foundation for Affordable Instruction and Tenancy Hope)
EIN: 33, 2640449
Tax Status: 501(c)(3) Public Charity
Service Area: South and Central Texas and the Texas Gulf Coast region, with primary focus on rural and underserved communities
Annual Organizational Budget: $75,000

FAITH Foundation exists to break the cycle of housing insecurity by providing financial education, homeownership instruction, and direct housing assistance to veterans, individuals experiencing homelessness, single parents, those in recovery, those reentering society, and other economically disadvantaged populations. Through our partnership with Bright Box Homes, we turn charitable giving into permanent, affordable housing solutions.

Reid Whitesides founded FAITH Foundation in Texas to address the critical shortage of affordable and transitional housing in rural South Texas communities, which is precisely the gap this funding opportunity was designed to close. The organization's three interconnected programs, the Down Payment Assistance Program, the Transitional Housing Program, and the Cornerstone Communities Initiative, together constitute a complete, supply, and, demand housing intervention. People enter in crisis. They leave with a home.

SECTION II: STATEMENT OF NEED

The Housing Crisis in Rural Texas

The affordable housing crisis in the United States is not a single problem. It's a compounding failure across multiple systems: a national shortage of 7.3 million rental units affordable to extremely low, income households, a homeownership market where the median age of first, time buyers has risen to a record 40 years old, and a down payment gap that locks out the families who would benefit most from the wealth, building stability of owning a home. In rural Texas, these failures are not theoretical. They are lived daily by the populations FAITH Foundation was created to serve.

Nearly 28,000 Texans were experiencing homelessness in the 2024 Point, in, Time count, including 1,837 veterans. Critically, 44% of Texans experiencing homelessness were unsheltered, meaning they had no access to emergency shelter or transitional housing of any kind. (HUD 2024 Annual Homelessness Assessment Report.) Chronic homelessness in Texas climbed from 1,949 individuals in 2022 to 2,594 in 2023, a 33% increase in a single year. (Texas Homeless Data Sharing Network.)

Those numbers are concentrated in communities where the nonprofit infrastructure to respond is thinnest: rural counties in South and Central Texas where affordable housing inventory is critically low, where transitional housing programs simply don't exist, and where the cost of traditional construction makes private development economically unviable.

The Populations This Grant Prioritizes, And Why They Are Underserved

Reentry Populations. Formerly incarcerated individuals are approximately 10 times more likely to experience homelessness than the general population. (National Low Income Housing Coalition; Prison Policy Initiative.) They make up between 23.1% and 47.8% of annual homeless shelter admissions. (Community Solutions / CSG Justice Center, 2019.) In Texas, a state that incarcerates at one of the highest rates in the nation, this translates to thousands of individuals released each year with no housing, no employment, and no transition plan. Research confirms that housing instability directly increases the risk of reincarceration through more frequent law enforcement contact and supervision violations tied to housing status. (CSG Justice Center, 2025.) Without stable transitional housing upon release, reentry becomes a revolving door. That's not a metaphor. It's what the data shows.

Individuals in Recovery. The relationship between housing instability and addiction is bidirectional and well, documented. People completing addiction treatment need immediate access to stable, sober housing to sustain their recovery. Without it, relapse rates climb and the investment in treatment is lost. Rural South Texas doesn't have an adequate supply of sober living and transitional recovery housing, which means treatment program graduates often return to the same unstable environments that preceded their addiction.

Veterans Experiencing Housing Insecurity. Texas has one of the highest concentrations of homeless veterans in the nation. In 2024, 1,837 veterans were counted as homeless in Texas, with a significant share unsheltered. (VA/HUD 2024 PIT Count.) Veteran homelessness in Texas did decrease 9.7% between 2023 and 2024, which matters. But that progress remains fragile and concentrated in urban areas, leaving rural veterans with limited access to VA services, transitional housing, or any path toward ownership.

The Rural Dimension. Rural South Texas faces acute housing shortages with limited nonprofit infrastructure. Traditional affordable housing development is cost, prohibitive in rural markets, and most existing housing assistance organizations concentrate their resources in San Antonio, Houston, or other urban centers. The populations FAITH Foundation serves, reentry, recovery, veterans, single parents, are present in rural communities but largely invisible to the housing systems designed around urban density. This is the gap FAITH Foundation was built to fill.

The Supply and Demand Failure

The data points to two interconnected failures that most organizations address only partially. There isn't enough housing inventory affordable to the populations we serve, and there isn't enough financial assistance to bridge the gap between rental instability and homeownership. FAITH Foundation addresses both: the demand side through direct down payment vouchers and housing counseling, and the supply side through the Cornerstone Communities land acquisition and modular housing development initiative. That integrated, both, sides approach, paired with a self, sustaining funding mechanism through the Bright Box Homes partnership, is what distinguishes FAITH Foundation from single, intervention housing programs.

SECTION III: PROGRAM DESIGN

Overview: An Integrated Three, Program Model

FAITH Foundation operates three interconnected housing programs across South and Central Texas, each addressing a distinct stage of the journey from housing crisis to permanent stability. This grant request supports all three programs, with funds targeted to the highest, priority activities aligned with CDBG, Housing priorities: down payment assistance for low, income families, transitional housing for reentry and recovery populations and veterans, and acquisition of modular housing units for Cornerstone Communities development.

Program 1: Down Payment Assistance Program

The Down Payment Assistance Program provides direct financial awards to qualifying low, income individuals and families to secure permanent housing. The program targets people who are employment, stable but lack savings for upfront housing costs, the precise population locked out of homeownership by the down payment gap documented above.

How It Works. Qualified applicants receive direct financial assistance toward down payments and rental security deposits. Awards are funded through a combination of grant resources, including CDBG, Housing funds requested here, and recurring contributions from the Bright Box Homes partnership, which donates $2,500 to the Foundation for every home sold. Paired with the Foundation's Financial Literacy program, Down Payment Assistance recipients receive pre, purchase counseling, mortgage readiness education, and budgeting support to make sure their transition to ownership actually holds.

Target Population. Priority goes to military veterans, individuals completing reentry programming, individuals in active recovery, and single, parent families, the funder's stated priority populations. Participants must demonstrate income eligibility and housing readiness through FAITH Foundation's case management assessment.

CDBG Alignment. This program directly addresses the funder's priority for down payment assistance for low, income families in rural Texas communities. Each dollar of CDBG investment is multiplied by the Bright Box Homes funding mechanism and paired with counseling and education services that increase the probability of long, term housing retention.

Program 2: Transitional Housing Program

The Transitional Housing Program places individuals exiting homelessness, incarceration, or addiction treatment into stable transitional units with case management support, financial literacy training, and peer mentorship for up to 24 months.

How It Works. FAITH Foundation coordinates with reentry service partners, recovery program partners, and veterans service organizations to identify individuals at the point of transition: upon release from incarceration, upon completion of addiction treatment, or upon discharge from a period of homelessness. Participants are placed into transitional housing and assigned to a case manager who maintains a maximum 15, to, 1 client ratio to ensure individualized support. Case management services include employment navigation, benefits enrollment coordination with county social services agencies and VA resources, financial literacy instruction, peer mentorship, and progressive goal, setting toward permanent housing placement.

Programmatic Structure. The program is structured as a progression, not a placement. Participants enter at a crisis or transitional stage and move through defined milestones toward independent, permanent housing. At entry, the focus is immediate stable housing, safety planning, needs assessment, and case management assignment. The stabilization phase covers employment establishment or benefits enrollment, debt management, financial literacy coursework, and recovery or reentry support group participation. From there, participants move into an advancement phase focused on credit, building, savings development, homeownership counseling enrollment, and down payment assistance application. Transition means permanent housing placement with 12, month post, placement follow, up and retention support.

CDBG Alignment. This program directly addresses the funder's stated priorities for transitional housing programs serving reentry populations, individuals in recovery, and veterans experiencing housing insecurity. FAITH Foundation's founder, Reid Whitesides, brings lived experience to every element of this program's design. He spent nearly twenty years incarcerated in Texas and has maintained sobriety for more than fifteen years. The program's peer mentorship model and case management structure reflect evidence, based practices documented by HUD and the VA for housing stability among high, barrier populations.

Program 3: Cornerstone Communities Initiative

The Cornerstone Communities Initiative is FAITH Foundation's flagship capital development program and the most direct response to the rural Texas housing supply crisis. The model acquires donated or reduced, cost land parcels in rural communities, then deploys modular and manufactured housing units, sourced through the Bright Box Homes partnership, to create purpose, built transitional micro, communities.

How It Works. Each Cornerstone Community consists of individual modular housing units sited on a single acquired land parcel, with shared community infrastructure including common spaces, case management facilities, community laundry, and where feasible, remote work and learning centers and shuttle transportation for rural access. Units are move, in, ready, durable, and cost, effective relative to traditional stick, built construction, making them well, suited for rural Texas deployment where construction costs and contractor availability would otherwise make development impossible.

FAITH Foundation acquires modular units through the Bright Box Homes partnership and through in, kind donations from building material suppliers and modular housing manufacturers. Land is acquired through donation from private landowners, churches, and municipalities, or purchased at reduced cost through established landowner partnerships in rural South Texas communities. Site preparation, utility infrastructure installation, and community common space construction are completed through competitive open, bid contracting, with oversight provided by Scott Ellis, FAITH Foundation's Board Chair and Treasurer. Scott has owned and led E4 Roofing & Construction in Georgetown, Texas for more than 15 years, and he brings that construction and financial management experience directly to bear on every capital project the Foundation undertakes.

The Rotating Model. As Cornerstone Communities residents stabilize and transition to permanent housing through the Foundation's Down Payment Assistance pipeline, their units become available for new participants. Each successful transition opens capacity for the next person in need, while the land and housing assets appreciate and reduce ongoing capital expenditure requirements over time.

On, Site Wraparound Services. Each Cornerstone Community is designed as more than a housing development. On, site programming includes recovery support groups, peer mentorship, financial literacy sessions, employment navigation, and case management, the full suite of FAITH Foundation's supportive services delivered where residents live. That matters in rural communities, where transportation is a real barrier and distance often determines whether someone gets help or doesn't.

CDBG Alignment. This program directly addresses the funder's stated priority for acquisition of modular housing units in rural Texas communities and development of affordable housing for low, income populations. The modular deployment model is specifically designed for rural Texas contexts where traditional affordable housing development fails. CDBG funds invested in Cornerstone Communities unit acquisition create permanent, appreciating housing assets that generate ongoing community impact well beyond the grant period.

Theory of Change

Stable housing is the prerequisite for sustained recovery from addiction, successful community reentry after incarceration, and long, term economic self, sufficiency. FAITH Foundation's model addresses the root cause of cyclical homelessness: the absence of affordable transitional housing in rural communities. By deploying modular housing units in purpose, built Cornerstone Communities, paired with case management, peer mentorship, financial literacy, and down payment assistance, individuals move through a structured pathway from crisis to stability to permanent housing. Each successful transition frees capacity for the next participant, and the cycle continues.

SECTION IV: ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY

Leadership and Governance

FAITH Foundation is governed by a board of directors whose combined experience in construction, finance, real estate, ministry, and community service directly equips the organization to manage federal funds, execute capital housing projects, and deliver the human services programming this grant supports.

Reid Whitesides, Founder and President, brings more than 20 years of experience in construction, roofing, project management, sales, consulting, and housing, related industries. His personal history, nearly twenty years incarcerated in the State of Texas and more than fifteen years of sustained sobriety, gives him direct, lived understanding of the barriers facing every population FAITH Foundation serves. He leads this organization with firsthand insight that no credential can replicate, and his construction and project management background ensures that Cornerstone Communities development is approached with real technical rigor.

Scott Ellis, Treasurer and Board Chair, is the owner of E4 Roofing & Construction in Georgetown, Texas, a company he has led for more than 15 years. Scott brings financial oversight, construction expertise, project coordination, budgeting, contractor management, and long, term asset stewardship to the Foundation's leadership. His 24 years as a Georgetown resident and his track record in residential and commercial construction provide directly applicable capacity for the capital development activities this grant funds. As Board Chair, Scott ensures that FAITH Foundation operates as a faithful steward of all resources entrusted to it, including federal grant funds.

Pastor Juan Valdez, Secretary and Protector, brings nearly 30 years of ordained ministry experience and a 34, year track record of business ownership. His hair studio, operated with his wife Martha, ran at the same San Antonio location for three and a half decades. That kind of longevity reflects something important: consistency, reliability, and a commitment to the community that doesn't waver when things get hard. Pastor Valdez provides governance accountability, mission stewardship, and the organizational grounding that sustained community presence requires. His international ministry experience spanning the United States, South America, Central America, the Caribbean, and Africa, combined with decades of local community service, reflects the same integrity FAITH Foundation brings to its housing work.

Financial Management

FAITH Foundation maintains its financial records in QuickBooks and operates with board, level financial oversight provided by Scott Ellis as Treasurer and Board Chair. The organization's annual operating budget is $75,000. Indirect costs are maintained below 15% of total program budget, with direct program delivery prioritized in all budget allocations. The Foundation's budget framework separates personnel, capital, and operating costs, and all in, kind donations of land, building materials, modular units, and professional services are documented at fair market value for matching fund purposes.

FAITH Foundation is prepared to meet all federal fund management requirements applicable to CDBG, Housing awards, including maintenance of segregated fund accounts for grant receipts and expenditures, quarterly financial reporting, and compliance with applicable procurement standards for capital expenditures.

Partnerships and Referral Networks

FAITH Foundation maintains active partnerships that directly support program delivery and participant referral across all three programs. Church partners provide volunteer labor, congregational fundraising, mentorship volunteers, and meeting space for participant programming. Recovery program partners refer individuals completing treatment who need stable transitional housing and provide ongoing support services for residents in active recovery. Reentry service partners coordinate with the Foundation to place formerly incarcerated individuals into transitional housing upon release, connecting them with employment services, legal aid, and family reunification support. County social services agencies and local housing authorities refer eligible families and individuals, coordinate benefits enrollment, and provide case management collaboration. Building material suppliers and modular housing manufacturers provide discounted or donated materials and units for Cornerstone Communities development. Landowners in rural South Texas communities donate or sell land at reduced cost for community development sites. Veterans service organizations refer military veterans experiencing housing insecurity and coordinate VA benefits enrollment. Bright Box Homes supplies the modular and manufactured housing units deployed in Cornerstone Communities and donates $2,500 per home sold to fund FAITH Foundation's housing voucher program.

This network enables the Foundation to pair its direct program investment with in, kind contributions, referral infrastructure, and co, delivered services that multiply the impact of every grant dollar.

Serving Rural Communities

Rural South Texas faces acute housing shortages with limited nonprofit infrastructure. FAITH Foundation addresses this through modular housing deployment: units can be sited on donated or acquired rural land without the delays and costs of traditional construction. That approach brings housing solutions directly to underserved rural communities rather than concentrating resources in urban centers. Program vehicles for rural case management outreach ensure that case managers can reach participants across geographically dispersed service areas. This rural, first design is embedded in every element of FAITH Foundation's program model, from the modular housing technology to the on, site service delivery structure of Cornerstone Communities.

SECTION V: INTENDED IMPACT AND EVALUATION

Intended Outcomes

FAITH Foundation is in its inaugural funding cycle. Initial operations have been funded through founder investment and church community support. The following outcomes represent the measurable targets the organization has set for its funded program period, informed by evidence, based models documented by HUD, the VA, and peer organizations operating comparable housing voucher and community development programs.

On housing placement and retention, the Foundation will track the number of individuals and families transitioned from homelessness or unstable housing into transitional units and permanent housing, tracked by 30,  60,  and 90, day retention rates, as well as the percentage of down payment assistance recipients maintaining stable housing at 12 months following award.

On financial stability, the Foundation will track the number of down payment assistance awards disbursed and average award amount, along with measured improvement in credit score, debt, to, income ratio, and savings rate among financial literacy program completers.

On reentry success, the Foundation will track the number of formerly incarcerated individuals housed through Transitional Housing and Cornerstone Communities programs, employment placement rate within 90 days of program enrollment, and recidivism reduction among program participants compared to regional averages.

On recovery outcomes, the Foundation will track the number of individuals in active recovery housed through the program, sobriety milestones maintained, and connection rates to ongoing treatment and support services at 12, month intervals.

On community development, the Foundation will track the number of Cornerstone Communities sites developed, total modular housing units acquired and placed, occupancy rates, and successful transitions from transitional to permanent housing.

How We Measure Success

All program data will be collected through FAITH Foundation's case management system and reported quarterly to the board of directors. Impact is measured across five domains: housing placement, financial stability, reentry success, recovery outcomes, and community development. All outcomes are tracked longitudinally with quarterly reporting and annual program evaluation. Annual impact reports will be published and made available to all funders, donors, and stakeholders. FAITH Foundation is committed to transparency in both financial stewardship and program outcomes and will pursue third, party outcome verification as program scale supports it.

Long, Term Sustainability

FAITH Foundation's long, term sustainability is built on a rotating housing asset model. Cornerstone Communities generate ongoing capacity as residents transition to permanent housing and units become available for new participants. Revenue streams include program fees assessed on a sliding scale based on participant income, rental income from stabilized housing units, recurring grant funding from federal, state, and private sources, corporate sponsorships and in, kind donations, church partnerships and congregational giving, and individual donor cultivation. Physical assets, land and modular housing units, appreciate over time and reduce ongoing capital expenditure requirements.

The Bright Box Homes partnership provides a private, sector, self, renewing revenue mechanism that isn't common among comparable organizations: $2,500 per Bright Box home sold flows directly into FAITH Foundation's down payment assistance voucher fund, creating a cycle of charitable investment that doesn't depend on annual reapplication. That mechanism, combined with diversified grant funding across government, foundation, corporate, and faith, based sources, is designed to prevent dependency on any single funding stream, including CDBG.

Operational costs are controlled through volunteer labor, donated materials, and shared administrative infrastructure across program sites. The Foundation actively pursues in, kind donations of land, building materials, modular and manufactured housing units, construction equipment and labor, furnishings, appliances, and professional services including legal, architectural, surveying, and construction management, all documented at fair market value and applied toward matching fund requirements where applicable.

SECTION VI: BUDGET NARRATIVE

FAITH Foundation's budget allocation for this grant prioritizes direct program delivery over administrative overhead, with indirect costs maintained below 15% of total program budget.

Personnel. Case managers maintaining a maximum 15, to, 1 client ratio and a housing navigator who coordinates placement across transitional and permanent housing options are the core of the personnel budget. These positions support the human infrastructure required to deliver case management, financial literacy instruction, and housing navigation to program participants. [NEEDS INPUT: specific personnel salary figures for this grant budget period]

Capital Expenditures, Modular Housing Unit Acquisition. Modular housing units for Cornerstone Communities are acquired at a cost of $30,000 to $60,000 per unit through the Foundation's Bright Box Homes partnership and open, market procurement. CDBG funds requested will be applied toward unit acquisition to maximize the number of transitional housing beds created per grant dollar. Site preparation and utility infrastructure installation costs are estimated separately and will be partially offset by in, kind contributions of construction labor and materials from church partners and building material donors.

Down Payment Assistance Awards. Direct financial assistance awards to qualifying individuals and families, disbursed in amounts to be determined by applicant need and program eligibility assessment. [NEEDS INPUT: specific per, award amount and number of awards budgeted for this grant period]

Operating Costs. Property maintenance, insurance, participant support services, transportation for rural case management outreach, and program supplies. Rural case management outreach requires dedicated transportation infrastructure given the geographic distribution of participants and program sites across South and Central Texas.

Indirect Costs. Organizational administration, accounting through QuickBooks, financial reporting, compliance, and grant management, maintained below 15% of total program budget.

In, Kind Match. FAITH Foundation documents in, kind contributions at fair market value, including donated land parcels, building materials, modular unit donations, construction labor, and professional services. These resources are applied toward matching fund requirements and reduce the cash outlay required per unit of housing created.

[NEEDS INPUT: completed line, item budget table with specific dollar amounts for each category for the grant period requested]

SECTION VII: ALIGNMENT WITH CDBG, HOUSING PRIORITIES

FAITH Foundation's three, program model maps directly and completely to each of the funder's stated priorities for this grant cycle.

On affordable housing development, the Cornerstone Communities Initiative responds through modular unit acquisition and site development on donated and acquired rural land. On transitional housing programs, the Transitional Housing Program provides up to 24, month transitional placement with case management, financial literacy, and peer mentorship. On down payment assistance for low, income families, the Down Payment Assistance Program delivers direct financial awards paired with homeownership counseling and financial literacy education. On acquisition of modular housing units in rural Texas, the Cornerstone Communities Initiative draws on the Bright Box Homes partnership for modular unit supply and a rural deployment model built specifically for this context. On reentry populations, the Second Chance Reentry component provides transitional housing, employment support, and case management for formerly incarcerated individuals. On individuals in recovery, the Recovery Housing component offers a structured continuum from transitional housing to permanent independent housing with on, site support. On veterans experiencing housing insecurity, the Veterans Path Home component delivers rental assistance, VA benefits navigation, and dedicated case management. On rural Texas communities, the Foundation's rural, first design deploys modular units to rural land, delivers services on, site, and maintains rural case management transportation infrastructure.

FAITH Foundation doesn't partially address these priorities. Its organizational mission, program design, target population, and geographic focus were established specifically for this nexus of need. The funder's priorities and FAITH Foundation's programs are not coincidentally aligned. They are structurally identical.

SECTION VIII: CERTIFICATION AND ATTACHMENTS

FAITH Foundation respectfully submits this narrative in support of its application to the Texas Community Development Block Grant, Housing program. The following required documents are included with this application: the 501(c)(3) determination letter (EIN: 33, 2640449), organizational budget, board of directors list, program narrative (this document), and budget narrative.

This is the gap FAITH Foundation was built to fill.

### The Supply and Demand Failure

The data reveals two interconnected failures that most organizations address only partially. First, there is insufficient housing inventory affordable to the populations we serve. Second, there is insufficient financial assistance to bridge the gap between rental instability and homeownership. FAITH Foundation addresses both: the demand side through direct down payment vouchers and housing counseling, and the supply side through our Cornerstone Communities land acquisition and modular housing development initiative. This integrated, both-sides approach — paired with a self-sustaining funding mechanism through our Bright Box Homes partnership — distinguishes FAITH Foundation from single-intervention housing programs.

---

## SECTION III: PROGRAM DESIGN

### Overview: An Integrated Three-Program Model

FAITH Foundation operates three interconnected housing programs across South and Central Texas, each addressing a distinct stage of the journey from housing crisis to permanent stability. This grant request supports all three programs, with funds targeted to the highest-priority activities aligned with CDBG-Housing priorities: down payment assistance for low-income families, transitional housing for reentry and recovery populations and veterans, and acquisition of modular housing units for Cornerstone Communities development.

---

### Program 1: Down Payment Assistance Program

The Down Payment Assistance Program provides direct financial awards to qualifying low-income individuals and families to secure permanent housing. The program targets individuals who are employment-stable but lack savings for upfront housing costs — the precise population locked out of homeownership by the down payment gap documented above.

**How It Works.** Qualified applicants receive direct financial assistance toward down payments and rental security deposits. Awards are funded through a combination of grant resources — including CDBG-Housing funds requested here — and recurring contributions from FAITH Foundation's partnership with Bright Box Homes, which donates $2,500 to the Foundation for every home sold. Paired with the Foundation's Financial Literacy program, Down Payment Assistance recipients receive pre-purchase counseling, mortgage readiness education, and budgeting support to ensure their transition to ownership is sustainable.

**Target Population.** Priority is given to military veterans, individuals completing reentry programming, individuals in active recovery, and single-parent families — the funder's stated priority populations. Participants must demonstrate income eligibility and housing readiness through FAITH Foundation's case management assessment.

**CDBG Alignment.** This program directly addresses the funder's priority for down payment assistance for low-income families in rural Texas communities. Each dollar of CDBG investment is multiplied by FAITH Foundation's Bright Box Homes funding mechanism and paired with counseling and education services that increase the probability of long-term housing retention.

---

### Program 2: Transitional Housing Program

The Transitional Housing Program places individuals exiting homelessness, incarceration, or addiction treatment into stable transitional units with case management support, financial literacy training, and peer mentorship for up to 24 months.

**How It Works.** FAITH Foundation coordinates with reentry service partners, recovery program partners, and veterans service organizations to identify individuals at the point of transition — upon release from incarceration, upon completion of addiction treatment, or upon discharge from a period of homelessness. Participants are placed into transitional housing and assigned to a case manager who maintains a maximum 15-to-1 client ratio to ensure individualized support. Case management services include employment navigation, benefits enrollment coordination with county social services agencies and VA resources, financial literacy instruction, peer mentorship, and progressive goal-setting toward permanent housing placement.

**Programmatic Structure.** The program is structured as a progression, not a placement. Participants enter at a crisis or transitional stage and move through defined milestones toward independent, permanent housing:

- **Entry:** Immediate stable housing, safety planning, needs assessment, and case management assignment
- **Stabilization:** Employment establishment or benefits enrollment, debt management, financial literacy coursework, recovery or reentry support group participation
- **Advancement:** Credit-building, savings development, homeownership counseling enrollment, down payment assistance application
- **Transition:** Permanent housing placement with 12-month post-placement follow-up and retention support

**CDBG Alignment.** This program directly addresses the funder's stated priorities for transitional housing programs serving reentry populations, individuals in recovery, and veterans experiencing housing insecurity. FAITH Foundation's founder, Reid Whitesides, brings lived experience — nearly twenty years incarcerated in Texas and more than fifteen years of sustained sobriety — that informs every element of this program's design. The program's peer mentorship model and case management structure reflect evidence-based practices documented by HUD and the VA for housing stability among high-barrier populations.

---

### Program 3: Cornerstone Communities Initiative

The Cornerstone Communities Initiative is FAITH Foundation's flagship capital development program and the most direct response to the rural Texas housing supply crisis. The model acquires donated or reduced-cost land parcels in rural communities, then deploys modular and manufactured housing units — sourced through the Foundation's strategic partnership with Bright Box Homes — to create purpose-built transitional micro-communities.

**How It Works.** Each Cornerstone Community consists of individual modular housing units sited on a single acquired land parcel, with shared community infrastructure including common spaces, case management facilities, community laundry, and where feasible, remote work and learning centers and shuttle transportation for rural access. Units are move-in-ready, durable, and cost-effective relative to traditional stick-built construction, making them uniquely suited for rural Texas deployment where construction costs and contractor availability would otherwise make development impossible.

FAITH Foundation acquires modular units through its partnership with Bright Box Homes and through in-kind donations from building material suppliers and modular housing manufacturers. Land is acquired through donation from private landowners, churches, and municipalities, or purchased at reduced cost through established landowner partnerships in rural South Texas communities. Site preparation, utility infrastructure installation, and community common space construction are completed through competitive open-bid contracting, with oversight provided by Scott Ellis, FAITH Foundation's Board Chair and Treasurer, who brings more than 15 years of experience as owner of E4 Roofing & Construction.

**The Rotating Model.** As Cornerstone Communities residents stabilize and transition to permanent housing through the Foundation's Down Payment Assistance pipeline, their units become available for new participants. This creates a self-sustaining cycle of community impact: each successful transition opens capacity for the next individual in need, while the land and housing assets appreciate and reduce ongoing capital expenditure requirements.

**On-Site Wraparound Services.** Each Cornerstone Community is designed as more than a housing development. On-site programming includes recovery support groups, peer mentorship, financial literacy sessions, employment navigation, and case management — the full suite of FAITH Foundation's supportive services delivered where residents live, removing transportation and access barriers common in rural communities.

**CDBG Alignment.** This program directly addresses the funder's stated priority for acquisition of modular housing units in rural Texas communities and development of affordable housing for low-income populations. The modular deployment model is specifically designed for rural Texas contexts where traditional affordable housing development fails. CDBG funds invested in Cornerstone Communities unit acquisition create permanent, appreciating housing assets that generate ongoing community impact far beyond the grant period.

---

### Theory of Change

Stable housing is the prerequisite for sustained recovery from addiction, successful community reentry after incarceration, and long-term economic self-sufficiency. FAITH Foundation's model addresses the root cause of cyclical homelessness — the absence of affordable transitional housing in rural communities. By deploying modular housing units in purpose-built Cornerstone Communities, paired with case management, peer mentorship, financial literacy, and down payment assistance, individuals progress through a structured pathway from crisis to stability to permanent housing. Each successful transition frees capacity for the next participant, creating a self-sustaining cycle of community impact.

---

## SECTION IV: ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY

### Leadership and Governance

FAITH Foundation is governed by a board of directors whose combined expertise in construction, finance, real estate, ministry, and community service directly equips the organization to manage federal funds, execute capital housing projects, and deliver the human services programming this grant supports.

**Reid Whitesides, Founder and President** brings more than 20 years of experience in construction, roofing, project management, sales, consulting, and housing-related industries. His personal experience — nearly twenty years incarcerated in the State of Texas and more than fifteen years of sustained sobriety — gives him direct, lived understanding of the barriers facing every population FAITH Foundation serves. He leads the organization with firsthand insight that no credential can replicate, and his construction and project management background ensures that Cornerstone Communities development is approached with technical rigor.

**Scott Ellis, Treasurer and Board Chair,** is the owner of E4 Roofing & Construction in Georgetown, Texas, which he has led for more than 15 years. Scott brings financial oversight, construction expertise, project coordination, budgeting, contractor management, and long-term asset stewardship to the Foundation's leadership. His 24 years as a Georgetown resident and his track record in residential and commercial construction provide direct, applicable capacity for the capital development activities this grant funds. As Board Chair, Scott ensures that FAITH Foundation operates as a faithful steward of all resources entrusted to it — including federal grant funds.

**Pastor Juan Valdez, Secretary and Protector,** brings nearly 30 years of ordained ministry experience and a 34-year track record of business ownership — his and his wife Martha's hair studio operated at the same San Antonio location for three and a half decades. Pastor Valdez provides governance accountability, mission stewardship, and the organizational consistency that sustained community presence requires. His international ministry experience and decades of community service reflect the same reliability and integrity FAITH Foundation brings to its housing work.

### Financial Management

FAITH Foundation maintains its financial records in QuickBooks and operates with board-level financial oversight provided by Scott Ellis as Treasurer and Board Chair. The organization's annual operating budget is $75,000. Indirect costs are maintained below 15% of total program budget, with direct program delivery prioritized in all budget allocations. The Foundation's budget framework separates personnel, capital, and operating costs, and all in-kind donations of land, building materials, modular units, and professional services are documented at fair market value for matching fund purposes.

FAITH Foundation is prepared to meet all federal fund management requirements applicable to CDBG-Housing awards, including maintenance of segregated fund accounts for grant receipts and expenditures, quarterly financial reporting, and compliance with applicable procurement standards for capital expenditures.

### Partnerships and Referral Networks

FAITH Foundation maintains active partnerships that directly support program delivery and participant referral across all three programs:

- **Church partners** provide volunteer labor, congregational fundraising, mentorship volunteers, and meeting space for participant programming
- **Recovery program partners** refer individuals completing treatment who need stable transitional housing and provide ongoing support services for residents in active recovery
- **Reentry service partners** coordinate with the Foundation to place formerly incarcerated individuals into transitional housing upon release, connecting them with employment services, legal aid, and family reunification support
- **County social services agencies and local housing authorities** refer eligible families and individuals, coordinate benefits enrollment, and provide case management collaboration
- **Building material suppliers and modular housing manufacturers** provide discounted or donated materials and units for Cornerstone Communities development
- **Landowners in rural South Texas communities** donate or sell land at reduced cost for community development sites
- **Veterans service organizations** refer military veterans experiencing housing insecurity and coordinate VA benefits enrollment
- **Bright Box Homes** supplies the modular and manufactured housing units deployed in the Foundation's Cornerstone Communities and donates $2,500 per home sold to fund FAITH Foundation's housing voucher program

This partnership network enables FAITH Foundation to leverage its direct program investment with in-kind contributions, referral infrastructure, and co-delivered services that multiply the impact of every grant dollar.

### Serving Rural Communities

Rural South Texas faces acute housing shortages with limited nonprofit infrastructure. FAITH Foundation addresses this through modular housing deployment — units can be sited on donated or acquired rural land without the delays and costs of traditional construction. This approach brings housing solutions directly to underserved rural communities rather than concentrating resources in urban centers. Program vehicles for rural case management outreach ensure that case managers can reach participants across geographically dispersed rural service areas. This rural-first design philosophy is embedded in every element of FAITH Foundation's program model, from the modular housing technology to the on-site service delivery structure of Cornerstone Communities.

---

## SECTION V: INTENDED IMPACT AND EVALUATION

### Intended Outcomes

FAITH Foundation is in its inaugural funding cycle. Initial operations have been funded through founder investment and church community support. The following outcomes represent the measurable targets the organization has set for its funded program period, informed by evidence-based models documented by HUD, the VA, and peer organizations operating comparable housing voucher and community development programs.

**Housing Placement and Retention**
- Number of individuals and families transitioned from homelessness or unstable housing into transitional units and permanent housing, tracked by 30-, 60-, and 90-day retention rates
- Percentage of down payment assistance recipients maintaining stable housing at 12 months following award

**Financial Stability**
- Number of down payment assistance awards disbursed and average award amount
- Measured improvement in credit score, debt-to-income ratio, and savings rate among financial literacy program completers

**Reentry Success**
- Number of formerly incarcerated individuals housed through Transitional Housing and Cornerstone Communities programs
- Employment placement rate within 90 days of program enrollment
- Recidivism reduction among program participants compared to regional averages

**Recovery Outcomes**
- Number of individuals in active recovery housed through the program
- Sobriety milestones maintained and connection rates to ongoing treatment and support services at 12-month intervals

**Community Development**
- Number of Cornerstone Communities sites developed
- Total modular housing units acquired and placed
- Occupancy rates and successful transitions from transitional to permanent housing

### How We Measure Success

All program data will be collected through FAITH Foundation's case management system and reported quarterly to the board of directors. Impact is measured across five domains: housing placement, financial stability, reentry success, recovery outcomes, and community development. All outcomes are tracked longitudinally with quarterly reporting and annual program evaluation. Annual impact reports will be published and made available to all funders, donors, and stakeholders. FAITH Foundation is committed to transparency in both financial stewardship and program outcomes and will pursue third-party outcome verification as program scale supports it.

### Long-Term Sustainability

FAITH Foundation's long-term sustainability is built on a rotating housing asset model. Cornerstone Communities generate ongoing capacity as residents transition to permanent housing and units become available for new participants. Revenue streams include program fees assessed on a sliding scale based on participant income, rental income from stabilized housing units, recurring grant funding from federal, state, and private sources, corporate sponsorships and in-kind donations, church partnerships and congregational giving, and individual donor cultivation. Physical assets — land and modular housing units — appreciate over time and reduce ongoing capital expenditure requirements.

The Foundation's partnership with Bright Box Homes provides a private-sector, self-renewing revenue mechanism not common among comparable organizations: $2,500 per Bright Box home sold flows directly into FAITH Foundation's down payment assistance voucher fund, creating a cycle of charitable investment that does not depend on annual reapplication. This mechanism, combined with diversified grant funding across government, foundation, corporate, and faith-based sources, is designed to prevent dependency on any single funding stream — including CDBG.

Operational costs are controlled through volunteer labor, donated materials, and shared administrative infrastructure across program sites. The Foundation actively pursues in-kind donations of land, building materials, modular and manufactured housing units, construction equipment and labor, furnishings, appliances, and professional services including legal, architectural, surveying, and construction management — all documented at fair market value and applied toward matching fund requirements where applicable.

---

## SECTION VI: BUDGET NARRATIVE

FAITH Foundation's budget allocation for this grant prioritizes direct program delivery over administrative overhead, with indirect costs maintained below 15% of total program budget.

**Personnel.** Case managers maintaining a maximum 15-to-1 client ratio and a housing navigator who coordinates placement across transitional and permanent housing options. Personnel costs support the human infrastructure required to deliver case management, financial literacy instruction, and housing navigation to program participants. [NEEDS INPUT: specific personnel salary figures for this grant budget period]

**Capital Expenditures — Modular Housing Unit Acquisition.** Modular housing units for Cornerstone Communities are acquired at a cost of $30,000 to $60,000 per unit through the Foundation's partnership with Bright Box Homes and open-market procurement. CDBG funds requested will be applied toward unit acquisition to maximize the number of transitional housing beds created per grant dollar. Site preparation and utility infrastructure installation costs are estimated separately and will be partially offset by in-kind contributions of construction labor and materials from church partners and building material donors.

**Down Payment Assistance Awards.** Direct financial assistance awards to qualifying individuals and families, disbursed in amounts to be determined by applicant need and program eligibility assessment. [NEEDS INPUT: specific per-award amount and number of awards budgeted for this grant period]

**Operating Costs.** Property maintenance, insurance, participant support services, transportation for rural case management outreach (program vehicles), and program supplies. Rural case management outreach requires dedicated transportation infrastructure given the geographic distribution of participants and program sites across South and Central Texas.

**Indirect Costs.** Organizational administration, accounting (QuickBooks), financial reporting, compliance, and grant management, maintained below 15% of total program budget.

**In-Kind Match.** FAITH Foundation actively documents in-kind contributions at fair market value, including donated land parcels, building materials, modular unit donations, construction labor, and professional services. These in-kind resources are applied toward matching fund requirements and reduce the cash outlay required per unit of housing created.

[NEEDS INPUT: completed line-item budget table with specific dollar amounts for each category for the grant period requested]

## SECTION VII: ALIGNMENT WITH CDBG-HOUSING PRIORITIES

FAITH Foundation's three-program model maps directly and completely to each of the funder's stated priorities for this grant cycle:

| **Funder Priority** | **FAITH Foundation Response** |
|---|---|
| Affordable housing development | Cornerstone Communities Initiative: modular unit acquisition and site development on donated/acquired rural land |
| Transitional housing programs | Transitional Housing Program: up to 24-month transitional placement with case management, financial literacy, and peer mentorship |
| Down payment assistance for low-income families | Down Payment Assistance Program: direct financial awards paired with homeownership counseling and financial literacy education |
| Acquisition of modular housing units in rural Texas | Cornerstone Communities Initiative: Bright Box Homes partnership for modular unit supply, rural deployment model |
| Reentry populations | Second Chance Reentry component: transitional housing, employment support, case management for formerly incarcerated individuals |
| Individuals in recovery | Recovery Housing component: structured continuum from transitional housing to permanent independent housing with on-site support |
| Veterans experiencing housing insecurity | Veterans Path Home component: rental assistance, VA benefits navigation, dedicated case management |
| Rural Texas communities | Rural-first design: modular deployment to rural land, on-site service delivery, rural case management transportation |

FAITH Foundation does not partially address these priorities. Its organizational mission, program design, target population, and geographic focus were established specifically for this nexus of need. The funder's priorities and FAITH Foundation's programs are not coincidentally aligned — they are structurally identical.

---

## SECTION VIII: CERTIFICATION AND ATTACHMENTS

FAITH Foundation respectfully submits this narrative in support of its application to the Texas Community Development Block Grant – Housing program. The following required documents are included with this application:

Texas Community Development Block Grant – Housing
Program Narrative
FAITH Foundation (EIN: 33, 2640449)

SECTION I: ORGANIZATIONAL OVERVIEW

FAITH Foundation, the Foundation for Affordable Instruction and Tenancy Hope, is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit headquartered in Texas. We exist to break the cycle of housing insecurity for the people most consistently shut out of stable, permanent housing. That means veterans, individuals experiencing homelessness, single parents, people in recovery, those reentering society after incarceration, and other economically disadvantaged populations who've been told, in practice if not in words, that homeownership isn't for them. Through our partnership with Bright Box Homes, we turn charitable giving into permanent, affordable housing solutions that last.

Founder and President Reid Whitesides established FAITH Foundation to address something he'd watched go unaddressed for years: the near, total absence of affordable and transitional housing options in rural South Texas communities. The conviction behind the organization is simple. Stable housing is the foundation for everything else, for recovery, for successful reentry, for economic self, sufficiency, and without it, every other intervention is temporary at best. Drawing on his background in construction, roofing, project management, and housing, related industries, Reid developed the Cornerstone Communities model, a practical approach to deploying affordable modular and manufactured housing at scale in rural areas where traditional development simply doesn't pencil out.

We serve South and Central Texas and the Texas Gulf Coast region, with primary focus on rural and underserved communities where affordable housing inventory is critically low and where the people we serve are most concentrated. The organization operates with an annual budget of $75,000 and maintains active partnerships with local churches, recovery programs, reentry service providers, county social services agencies, local housing authorities, modular housing manufacturers, building material suppliers, and veterans service organizations across South Texas.

SECTION II: STATEMENT OF NEED

The Rural Texas Housing Crisis

Rural South Texas communities are dealing with a housing crisis that compounds on itself. The absence of affordable transitional and permanent housing options, combined with limited nonprofit infrastructure, geographic isolation, and concentrated populations of veterans, formerly incarcerated individuals, and people in active recovery, creates conditions where housing instability becomes chronic rather than episodic. People don't fall into a hole and climb back out. They fall in, and there's nothing to grab onto.

The scale of this is documented, not estimated. Nearly 28,000 Texans were experiencing homelessness in the 2024 Point, in, Time count, including 1,837 veterans, and 44% of that population was entirely unsheltered, meaning no emergency shelter, no transitional housing, nothing. (HUD 2024 Annual Homelessness Assessment Report.) Chronic homelessness in Texas jumped from 1,949 individuals in 2022 to 2,594 in 2023, a 33% increase in a single year, driven in significant part by the absence of transitional housing capacity to interrupt the cycle before it becomes permanent. (Texas Homeless Data Sharing Network.)

For the three priority populations this grant opportunity specifically identifies, reentry populations, individuals in recovery, and veterans experiencing housing insecurity, the crisis is acute and well, documented.

Reentry. Formerly incarcerated individuals are approximately 10 times more likely to experience homelessness than the general population. (National Low Income Housing Coalition / Prison Policy Initiative.) They account for between 23.1% and 47.8% of annual homeless shelter admissions nationally. (Community Solutions / CSG Justice Center, 2019.) Research demonstrates that housing instability after release dramatically increases the risk of reincarceration: 82% of individuals released from prison across 24 states were re, arrested within 10 years of release, and the absence of stable housing is a primary driver. (UNLV Reentry Research Brief, 2024.) Texas releases tens of thousands of individuals from state correctional facilities annually. The rural communities of South Texas have virtually no dedicated transitional housing infrastructure to receive them.

Recovery. Individuals completing addiction treatment face an immediate, documented housing crisis upon discharge. Without stable, sober housing, relapse risk increases sharply and the investment of treatment is lost. The rural South Texas communities FAITH Foundation serves lack sober living facilities, recovery housing, and the structured transitional continuum that bridges treatment completion and independent living. Our Recovery Housing program provides a structured path from sober living through transitional housing to permanent independent placement, with on, site support groups and accountability at every stage, and it directly fills this gap.

Veterans. Texas has one of the highest concentrations of homeless veterans in the nation. In 2024, 1,837 veterans were experiencing homelessness in Texas. Veteran homelessness did decline 9.7% between 2023 and 2024, progress directly attributable to targeted housing interventions. (VA/HUD 2024 PIT Count.) But rural veterans face a distinct disadvantage: VA services, benefits navigation, and housing support are concentrated in urban centers, leaving rural veterans without the infrastructure to access the benefits they earned. FAITH Foundation's Veterans Path Home program brings rental assistance, VA benefits navigation, and dedicated case management directly to veterans in underserved rural communities.

The Rural Supply Gap

Beyond demand, side barriers, rural South Texas faces a structural supply, side failure. There is simply not enough affordable housing inventory to meet existing need, regardless of residents' financial resources. The national shortage of 7.3 million rental units affordable and available to extremely low, income households is disproportionately concentrated in rural communities where development economics make traditional affordable housing construction unprofitable and where nonprofit housing developers have historically not operated. (National Low Income Housing Coalition.)

This is the specific gap FAITH Foundation was founded to fill. Modular and manufactured housing units deployed on acquired or donated land in purpose, built Cornerstone Communities bring affordable housing supply directly to rural communities without the cost structure, timelines, or infrastructure dependencies of traditional construction. No other organization in our service area provides this integrated supply, and, demand approach to rural affordable housing.

The Down Payment Barrier

For individuals who achieve housing stability and seek to transition to permanent homeownership, one final barrier remains. The median age of first, time homebuyers has climbed to a record 40 years old, and first, time buyers now represent just 21% of the market, the lowest share since the National Association of Realtors began tracking in 1981. Sixty, seven percent of millennials have no savings for a home down payment. (REsimpli 2025 Market Survey.) For individuals rebuilding from incarceration, addiction, or chronic homelessness, that challenge is exponentially greater. FAITH Foundation's Down Payment Assistance Program provides direct financial awards that bridge this final gap and convert program participants from transitional residents into permanent homeowners.

SECTION III: PROGRAM DESIGN

Overview

FAITH Foundation requests funding under the Texas Community Development Block Grant – Housing to support three interconnected program components aligned directly with this grant's stated priorities: transitional housing programming for reentry, recovery, and veteran populations; down payment assistance for low, income families; and acquisition of modular housing units for deployment in rural Cornerstone Communities sites.

These three components are not independent initiatives. They form a structured continuum. Participants enter through transitional housing, receive case management and financial literacy services during their stay, and exit through down payment assistance into permanent homeownership. Each successful transition creates capacity for the next participant, generating a self, sustaining cycle of community impact.

Component 1: Transitional Housing Program

FAITH Foundation's Transitional Housing Program places individuals exiting homelessness, incarceration, or addiction treatment into stable transitional units with case management support, financial literacy training, and peer mentorship for up to 24 months. The program serves three priority populations that align directly with this grant opportunity's stated priorities.

Second Chance Reentry Housing provides transitional housing, employment support, and case management for formerly incarcerated individuals rebuilding stability after release. Reentry service partners coordinate with FAITH Foundation to place individuals upon release, connecting them with employment services, legal aid, and family reunification support. Case managers maintain a maximum 15, to, 1 client ratio to ensure individualized attention and accountability.

Recovery Housing provides a structured continuum from sober living through transitional housing to permanent independent living, with on, site support groups and accountability at every stage. Recovery program partners refer individuals completing treatment who need stable transitional housing and provide ongoing support services for residents in active recovery. This program directly addresses the documented housing gap between treatment completion and independent living that drives relapse in rural communities.

Veterans Path Home provides rental assistance, VA benefits navigation, and dedicated case management for military veterans transitioning from housing instability to permanent homes. Veterans service organization partners refer military veterans experiencing housing insecurity and coordinate VA benefits enrollment. For rural veterans with limited access to urban VA infrastructure, FAITH Foundation serves as the primary bridge between their eligibility and the benefits they've earned.

All three transitional housing streams operate under an identical case management framework. Upon entry, each participant completes a full housing and stability assessment. A personalized housing plan is developed with specific 30,  60,  and 90, day milestones. Case managers conduct weekly individual check, ins and connect participants to employer partners, financial literacy programming, and peer mentorship. Progress is documented in FAITH Foundation's case management system and reported quarterly to the board of directors.

Component 2: Down Payment Assistance Program

The Down Payment Assistance Program provides direct financial awards to qualifying low, income individuals and families to secure permanent housing. It targets individuals who've achieved employment stability and completed FAITH Foundation's financial literacy curriculum but lack savings for upfront housing costs, that last barrier between transitional and permanent housing.

Eligibility criteria prioritize the populations identified in this grant opportunity: veterans, individuals in recovery, and those reentering from incarceration, as well as single, parent families and individuals transitioning out of homelessness. Award amounts of $2,500 per household are provided as direct housing assistance, funded through a combination of grant awards, the Foundation's partnership with Bright Box Homes (which donates $2,500 for every home sold), and other contributed revenue.

Financial literacy education is a prerequisite for all Down Payment Assistance recipients. FAITH Foundation's Financial Literacy program provides hands, on budgeting, credit, building, and debt management education that prepares families to qualify for and sustain homeownership. Requiring completion of this curriculum before award disbursement ensures that down payment assistance is matched by the financial readiness to sustain homeownership long, term.

Component 3: Modular Housing Unit Acquisition, Cornerstone Communities Initiative

The Cornerstone Communities Initiative is FAITH Foundation's flagship development program and its most direct response to the rural housing supply crisis. The Foundation acquires donated or reduced, cost land from private owners, churches, municipalities, and landowners in rural South Texas communities, then deploys modular and manufactured housing units through its partnership with Bright Box Homes to create purpose, built transitional micro, communities.

Each Cornerstone Community includes individual housing units, shared community spaces, and on, site access to case management and support services including recovery programming, remote work and learning centers, community laundry facilities, shuttle transportation for rural outreach, and dedicated case management. Residents enter as transitional housing participants and graduate into permanent homeownership through FAITH Foundation's voucher and down payment assistance pipeline.

Modular housing units are acquired through the Foundation's partnership with Bright Box Homes, which supplies the modular and manufactured units deployed in Cornerstone Communities, enabling charitable contributions to be converted directly into durable, move, in, ready homes. Unit costs range from $30,000 to $60,000 per unit inclusive of site preparation and utility infrastructure. That cost structure is dramatically lower than traditional affordable housing development and makes it feasible to bring permanent affordable housing supply to rural communities that conventional development economics have bypassed.

CDBG funding directed to this component will support the acquisition of modular housing units for deployment at Cornerstone Communities sites in rural South Texas, directly increasing the stock of affordable transitional housing available to veterans, reentry, and recovery populations in communities with critical supply shortages.

Program Delivery Model

FAITH Foundation's model addresses both sides of the rural affordable housing crisis at the same time: the demand side through direct down payment vouchers, financial literacy, and case management, and the supply side through the Cornerstone Communities land acquisition and modular unit deployment initiative. Participants may enter the FAITH Foundation ecosystem through any program door and are supported through a structured pathway from crisis to stability to permanent housing.

The Foundation's theory of change is grounded in evidence: stable housing is the prerequisite for sustained recovery from addiction, successful community reentry after incarceration, and long, term economic self, sufficiency. By deploying modular housing units in purpose, built Cornerstone Communities, paired with case management, peer mentorship, financial literacy, and down payment assistance, individuals move through a structured pathway from crisis to stability to permanent housing. Each successful transition frees capacity for the next participant, creating a self, sustaining cycle of community impact.

SECTION IV: ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY

Leadership and Governance

FAITH Foundation is governed by a board of directors whose collective expertise in construction, financial management, housing industry practice, and community service directly supports the Foundation's mission and its capacity to manage federal funds responsibly.

Reid Whitesides, Founder and President, brings more than 20 years of experience in construction, roofing, project management, sales, consulting, and housing, related industries. His commitment to this work isn't abstract. During a long struggle with addiction, Reid spent nearly twenty years incarcerated in the State of Texas, an experience that gave him firsthand insight into the barriers individuals face when rebuilding their lives after addiction, incarceration, and homelessness. Today, he's been sober for more than fifteen years. His lived experience, combined with his professional expertise, gives FAITH Foundation a leader who understands both the urgency of this work and the practical mechanics of housing development, construction, and program management.

Scott Ellis, Treasurer and Board Chair, is the owner of E4 Roofing & Construction, a Georgetown, Texas, based company he's led for more than 15 years. Scott's experience in residential and commercial construction, project coordination, budgeting, contractor management, and building systems gives FAITH Foundation directly applicable construction and housing industry expertise. His financial management experience as a business owner ensures the Foundation approaches grant funds with the accountability and stewardship expected of federal fund recipients, and his understanding of construction costs, building practices, and long, term asset stewardship means Cornerstone Communities projects are executed responsibly and efficiently.

Pastor Juan Valdez, Secretary and Protector, brings nearly 30 years of ordained ministry experience and a lifetime of community leadership to the Foundation's governance structure. His 34, year history of successful business ownership in San Antonio, operating a hair studio at the same location for three decades, reflects the consistency, reliability, and stewardship that characterize his role in Foundation governance. Pastor Valdez provides spiritual oversight, governance accountability, and mission stewardship, ensuring the Foundation remains faithful to its founding purpose and operates with integrity.

Financial Management

FAITH Foundation maintains its financial records using QuickBooks and operates with an annual organizational budget of $75,000. The Foundation is committed to maintaining indirect costs below 15% of total program budget. Financial oversight is provided by Treasurer and Board Chair Scott Ellis, whose 15, year history of business ownership provides demonstrated capacity for financial stewardship and accountability. The Foundation's budget allocation prioritizes direct program delivery, with personnel costs supporting case managers at a maximum 15, to, 1 client ratio and a housing navigator who coordinates placement across transitional and permanent housing options.

FAITH Foundation is in its inaugural funding cycle, with initial operations funded through founder investment and church community support. The organization actively pursues diversified funding across government grants, private foundations, corporate giving programs, faith, based funders, and community development financial institutions to avoid dependency on any single source, a funding structure consistent with responsible management of federal CDBG funds.

Program Infrastructure

FAITH Foundation's program infrastructure directly supports its capacity to manage and deliver results with CDBG funding.
