Texas Community Development Block Grant – Housing
Program Narrative
FAITH Foundation (EIN: 33, 2640449)

SECTION I: ORGANIZATIONAL OVERVIEW

FAITH Foundation, the Foundation for Affordable Instruction and Tenancy Hope, is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization headquartered in Texas. We exist to break the cycle of housing insecurity for the people most consistently shut out of stable, permanent housing. That means veterans, individuals experiencing homelessness, single parents, people in recovery, those reentering society after incarceration, and other economically disadvantaged populations who've been told, in practice if not in words, that homeownership isn't for them. Through our partnership with Bright Box Homes, we turn charitable giving into permanent, affordable housing solutions that last.

Founder and President Reid Whitesides established FAITH Foundation to address something he'd watched go unaddressed for years: the near, total absence of affordable and transitional housing options in rural South Texas communities. The conviction behind the organization is straightforward. Stable housing is the foundation for everything else, for recovery, for successful reentry, for economic self, sufficiency, and without it, every other intervention is temporary at best. Drawing on the founder's background in construction, roofing, project management, and housing, related industries, FAITH Foundation developed the Cornerstone Communities model, a practical approach to deploying affordable modular and manufactured housing at scale in rural areas where traditional development simply doesn't pencil out.

We serve South and Central Texas and the Texas Gulf Coast region, with primary focus on rural and underserved communities where affordable housing inventory is critically low and where the people we serve are most concentrated. The organization operates with an annual budget of $75,000 and maintains active partnerships with local churches, recovery programs, reentry service providers, county social services agencies, local housing authorities, modular housing manufacturers, building material suppliers, and veterans service organizations across South Texas.

SECTION II: STATEMENT OF NEED

The Rural Texas Housing Crisis

Rural South Texas communities are dealing with a housing crisis that compounds on itself. The absence of affordable transitional and permanent housing options, combined with limited nonprofit infrastructure, geographic isolation, and concentrated populations of veterans, formerly incarcerated individuals, and people in active recovery, creates conditions where housing instability becomes chronic rather than episodic. People don't fall into a hole and climb back out. They fall in, and there's nothing to grab onto.

The scale of this is documented, not estimated. Nearly 28,000 Texans were experiencing homelessness in the 2024 Point, in, Time count, including 1,837 veterans. Forty, four percent of Texans experiencing homelessness were unsheltered, meaning they had no access to emergency shelter or transitional housing of any kind. (HUD 2024 Annual Homelessness Assessment Report.) Chronic homelessness in Texas jumped from 1,949 individuals in 2022 to 2,594 in 2023, a 33% increase in a single year, driven in significant part by the absence of transitional housing capacity to interrupt the cycle before it becomes permanent. (Texas Homeless Data Sharing Network.)

For the three priority populations this grant opportunity specifically identifies, reentry populations, individuals in recovery, and veterans experiencing housing insecurity, the crisis is acute and well, documented.

Reentry. Formerly incarcerated individuals are approximately 10 times more likely to experience homelessness than the general population. (National Low Income Housing Coalition / Prison Policy Initiative.) They account for between 23.1% and 47.8% of annual homeless shelter admissions nationally. (Community Solutions / CSG Justice Center, 2019.) Research demonstrates that housing instability after release dramatically increases the risk of reincarceration: 82% of individuals released from prison across 24 states were re, arrested within 10 years of release, and the absence of stable housing is a primary driver. (UNLV Reentry Research Brief, 2024.) Texas releases tens of thousands of individuals from state correctional facilities annually. The rural communities of South Texas have virtually no dedicated transitional housing infrastructure to receive them.

Recovery. Individuals completing addiction treatment face an immediate, documented housing crisis upon discharge. Without stable, sober housing, relapse risk increases sharply and the investment of treatment is lost. The rural South Texas communities FAITH Foundation serves lack sober living facilities, recovery housing, and the structured transitional continuum that bridges treatment completion and independent living. Our Recovery Housing program, which provides structured transitional housing from sober living through permanent independent placement with on, site support groups and accountability, directly fills this gap.

Veterans. Texas has one of the highest concentrations of homeless veterans in the nation. In 2024, 1,837 veterans were experiencing homelessness in Texas. Veteran homelessness did decline 9.7% between 2023 and 2024, progress directly attributable to targeted housing interventions. (VA/HUD 2024 PIT Count.) But rural veterans face a distinct disadvantage: VA services, benefits navigation, and housing support are concentrated in urban centers, leaving rural veterans without the infrastructure to access the benefits they earned. FAITH Foundation's Veterans Path Home program brings rental assistance, VA benefits navigation, and dedicated case management directly to veterans in underserved rural communities.

The Rural Supply Gap

Beyond demand, side barriers, rural South Texas faces a structural supply, side failure. There is simply not enough affordable housing inventory to meet existing need, regardless of residents' financial resources. The national shortage of 7.3 million rental units affordable and available to extremely low, income households is disproportionately concentrated in rural communities where development economics make traditional affordable housing construction unprofitable and where nonprofit housing developers have historically not operated. (National Low Income Housing Coalition.)

This is the specific gap FAITH Foundation was founded to fill. Modular and manufactured housing units deployed on acquired or donated land in purpose, built Cornerstone Communities bring affordable housing supply directly to rural communities without the cost structure, timelines, or infrastructure dependencies of traditional construction. No other organization in our service area provides this integrated, supply, and, demand approach to rural affordable housing.

The Down Payment Barrier

For individuals who achieve housing stability and seek to transition to permanent homeownership, one final barrier remains. The median age of first, time homebuyers has climbed to a record 40 years old, and first, time buyers now represent just 21% of the market, the lowest share since the National Association of Realtors began tracking in 1981. Sixty, seven percent of millennials have no savings for a home down payment. (REsimpli 2025 Market Survey.) For individuals rebuilding from incarceration, addiction, or chronic homelessness, that challenge is exponentially greater. FAITH Foundation's Down Payment Assistance Program provides direct financial awards that bridge this final gap and convert program participants from transitional residents into permanent homeowners.

SECTION III: PROGRAM DESIGN

Overview

FAITH Foundation requests funding under the Texas Community Development Block Grant – Housing to support three interconnected program components aligned directly with this grant's stated priorities: transitional housing programming for reentry, recovery, and veteran populations; down payment assistance for low, income families; and acquisition of modular housing units for deployment in rural Cornerstone Communities sites.

These three components are not independent initiatives. They form a structured continuum. Participants enter through transitional housing, receive case management and financial literacy services during their stay, and exit through down payment assistance into permanent homeownership. Each successful transition creates capacity for the next participant, generating a self, sustaining cycle of community impact.

Component 1: Transitional Housing Program

FAITH Foundation's Transitional Housing Program places individuals exiting homelessness, incarceration, or addiction treatment into stable transitional units with case management support, financial literacy training, and peer mentorship for up to 24 months. The program serves three priority populations that align directly with this grant opportunity's stated priorities.

Second Chance Reentry Housing provides transitional housing, employment support, and case management for formerly incarcerated individuals rebuilding stability after release. Reentry service partners coordinate with FAITH Foundation to place individuals upon release, connecting them with employment services, legal aid, and family reunification support. Case managers maintain a maximum 15, to, 1 client ratio to ensure individualized attention and accountability.

Recovery Housing provides a structured continuum from sober living through transitional housing to permanent independent living, with on, site support groups and accountability at every stage. Recovery program partners refer individuals completing treatment who need stable transitional housing and provide ongoing support services for residents in active recovery. This program directly addresses the documented housing gap between treatment completion and independent living that drives relapse in rural communities.

Veterans Path Home provides rental assistance, VA benefits navigation, and dedicated case management for military veterans transitioning from housing instability to permanent homes. Veterans service organization partners refer military veterans experiencing housing insecurity and coordinate VA benefits enrollment. For rural veterans with limited access to urban VA infrastructure, FAITH Foundation serves as the primary bridge between their eligibility and the benefits they've earned.

All three transitional housing streams operate under an identical case management framework. Upon entry, each participant completes a complete housing and stability assessment. A personalized housing plan is developed with specific 30,  60,  and 90, day milestones. Case managers conduct weekly individual check, ins and connect participants to employer partners, financial literacy programming, and peer mentorship. Progress is documented in FAITH Foundation's case management system and reported quarterly to the board of directors.

Component 2: Down Payment Assistance Program

The Down Payment Assistance Program provides direct financial awards to qualifying low, income individuals and families to secure permanent housing. It targets individuals who've achieved employment stability and completed FAITH Foundation's financial literacy curriculum but lack savings for upfront housing costs, that last barrier between transitional and permanent housing.

Eligibility criteria prioritize the populations identified in this grant opportunity: veterans, individuals in recovery, and those reentering from incarceration, as well as single, parent families and individuals transitioning out of homelessness. Award amounts of $2,500 per household are provided as direct housing assistance, funded through a combination of grant awards, the Foundation's partnership with Bright Box Homes (which donates $2,500 for every home sold), and other contributed revenue.

Financial literacy education is a prerequisite for all Down Payment Assistance recipients. FAITH Foundation's Financial Literacy program provides hands, on budgeting, credit, building, and debt management education that prepares families to qualify for and sustain homeownership. Requiring completion of this curriculum before award disbursement ensures that down payment assistance is matched by the financial readiness to sustain homeownership long, term.

Component 3: Modular Housing Unit Acquisition, Cornerstone Communities Initiative

The Cornerstone Communities Initiative is FAITH Foundation's flagship development program and its most direct response to the rural housing supply crisis. The Foundation acquires donated or reduced, cost land from private owners, churches, municipalities, and landowners in rural South Texas communities, then deploys modular and manufactured housing units through its partnership with Bright Box Homes to create purpose, built transitional micro, communities.

Each Cornerstone Community includes individual housing units, shared community spaces, and on, site access to case management and support services including recovery programming, remote work and learning centers, community laundry facilities, shuttle transportation for rural outreach, and dedicated case management. Residents enter as transitional housing participants and graduate into permanent homeownership through FAITH Foundation's voucher and down payment assistance pipeline.

Modular housing units are acquired through the Foundation's partnership with Bright Box Homes, which supplies the modular and manufactured units deployed in Cornerstone Communities, enabling charitable contributions to be converted directly into durable, move, in, ready homes. Unit costs range from $30,000 to $60,000 per unit inclusive of site preparation and utility infrastructure. That cost structure is dramatically lower than traditional affordable housing development and makes it feasible to bring permanent affordable housing supply to rural communities that conventional development economics have bypassed.

CDBG funding directed to this component will support the acquisition of modular housing units for deployment at Cornerstone Communities sites in rural South Texas, directly increasing the stock of affordable transitional housing available to veterans, reentry, and recovery populations in communities with critical supply shortages.

Program Delivery Model

FAITH Foundation's model addresses both sides of the rural affordable housing crisis at the same time: the demand side through direct down payment vouchers, financial literacy, and case management, and the supply side through the Cornerstone Communities land acquisition and modular unit deployment initiative. Participants may enter the FAITH Foundation ecosystem through any program door and are supported through a structured pathway from crisis to stability to permanent housing.

The Foundation's theory of change is grounded in evidence: stable housing is the prerequisite for sustained recovery from addiction, successful community reentry after incarceration, and long, term economic self, sufficiency. By deploying modular housing units in purpose, built Cornerstone Communities, paired with case management, peer mentorship, financial literacy, and down payment assistance, individuals move through a structured pathway from crisis to stability to permanent housing. Each successful transition frees capacity for the next participant, creating a self, sustaining cycle of community impact.

### The Down Payment Barrier

For individuals who achieve housing stability and seek to transition to permanent homeownership, a final barrier remains: the down payment gap. The median age of first-time homebuyers has climbed to a record 40 years old, and first-time buyers now represent just 21% of the market — the lowest share since the National Association of Realtors began tracking in 1981. Sixty-seven percent of millennials have no savings for a home down payment. (REsimpli 2025 Market Survey.) For individuals rebuilding from incarceration, addiction, or chronic homelessness, the challenge is exponentially greater. FAITH Foundation's Down Payment Assistance Program provides direct financial awards that bridge this final gap and convert program participants from transitional residents into permanent homeowners.

---

## SECTION III: PROGRAM DESIGN

### Overview

FAITH Foundation requests funding under the Texas Community Development Block Grant – Housing to support three interconnected program components aligned directly with this grant's stated priorities: (1) transitional housing programming for reentry, recovery, and veteran populations; (2) down payment assistance for low-income families; and (3) acquisition of modular housing units for deployment in rural Cornerstone Communities sites.

These three components are not independent initiatives — they form a structured continuum. Participants enter through transitional housing, receive case management and financial literacy services during their stay, and exit through down payment assistance into permanent homeownership. Each successful transition creates capacity for the next participant, generating a self-sustaining cycle of community impact.

### Component 1: Transitional Housing Program

FAITH Foundation's Transitional Housing Program places individuals exiting homelessness, incarceration, or addiction treatment into stable transitional units with case management support, financial literacy training, and peer mentorship for up to 24 months. The program serves three priority populations that align directly with this grant opportunity's stated priorities:

**Second Chance Reentry Housing:** Transitional housing, employment support, and case management for formerly incarcerated individuals rebuilding stability after release. Reentry service partners coordinate with FAITH Foundation to place individuals upon release, connecting them with employment services, legal aid, and family reunification support. Case managers maintain a maximum 15-to-1 client ratio to ensure individualized attention and accountability.

**Recovery Housing:** A structured continuum from sober living through transitional housing to permanent independent living, with on-site support groups and accountability at every stage. Recovery program partners refer individuals completing treatment who need stable transitional housing, and provide ongoing support services for residents in active recovery. This program directly addresses the documented housing gap between treatment completion and independent living that drives relapse in rural communities.

**Veterans Path Home:** Rental assistance, VA benefits navigation, and dedicated case management for military veterans transitioning from housing instability to permanent homes. Veterans service organization partners refer military veterans experiencing housing insecurity and coordinate VA benefits enrollment. For rural veterans with limited access to urban VA infrastructure, FAITH Foundation serves as the primary bridge between their eligibility and the benefits they have earned.

All three transitional housing streams operate under an identical case management framework. Upon entry, each participant completes a comprehensive housing and stability assessment. A personalized housing plan is developed with specific 30-, 60-, and 90-day milestones. Case managers conduct weekly individual check-ins and connect participants to employer partners, financial literacy programming, and peer mentorship. Progress is documented in FAITH Foundation's case management system and reported quarterly to the board of directors.

### Component 2: Down Payment Assistance Program

The Down Payment Assistance Program provides direct financial awards to qualifying low-income individuals and families to secure permanent housing. The program targets individuals who have achieved employment stability and completed FAITH Foundation's financial literacy curriculum but lack savings for upfront housing costs — the final barrier between transitional and permanent housing.

Eligibility criteria prioritize the populations identified in this grant opportunity: veterans, individuals in recovery, and those reentering from incarceration, as well as single-parent families and individuals transitioning out of homelessness. Award amounts of $2,500 per household are provided as direct housing assistance, funded through a combination of grant awards, the Foundation's partnership with Bright Box Homes — which donates $2,500 for every home sold — and other contributed revenue.

Financial literacy education is a prerequisite for all Down Payment Assistance award recipients. FAITH Foundation's Financial Literacy program provides hands-on budgeting, credit-building, and debt management education that prepares families to qualify for and sustain homeownership. By requiring completion of this curriculum prior to award disbursement, the Foundation ensures that down payment assistance is matched by the financial readiness to sustain homeownership long-term.

### Component 3: Modular Housing Unit Acquisition — Cornerstone Communities Initiative

The Cornerstone Communities Initiative is FAITH Foundation's flagship development program and its most direct response to the rural housing supply crisis. The Foundation acquires donated or reduced-cost land from private owners, churches, municipalities, and landowners in rural South Texas communities, then deploys modular and manufactured housing units through its strategic partnership with Bright Box Homes to create purpose-built transitional micro-communities.

Each Cornerstone Community includes individual housing units, shared community spaces, and on-site access to case management and support services including recovery programming, remote work and learning centers, community laundry facilities, shuttle transportation for rural outreach, and dedicated case management. Residents enter as transitional housing participants and graduate into permanent homeownership through FAITH Foundation's voucher and down payment assistance pipeline.

Modular housing units are acquired through the Foundation's partnership with Bright Box Homes, which supplies the modular and manufactured units deployed in Cornerstone Communities, enabling charitable contributions to be converted directly into durable, move-in-ready homes. Unit costs range from $30,000 to $60,000 per unit inclusive of site preparation and utility infrastructure. This cost structure is dramatically lower than traditional affordable housing development and makes it feasible to bring permanent affordable housing supply to rural communities that have been bypassed by conventional development economics.

CDBG funding directed to this component will support the acquisition of modular housing units for deployment at Cornerstone Communities sites in rural South Texas, directly increasing the stock of affordable transitional housing available to veterans, reentry, and recovery populations in communities with critical supply shortages.

### Program Delivery Model

FAITH Foundation's model addresses both sides of the rural affordable housing crisis simultaneously: the demand side through direct down payment vouchers, financial literacy, and case management; and the supply side through the Cornerstone Communities land acquisition and modular unit deployment initiative. Participants may enter the FAITH Foundation ecosystem through any program door and are supported through a structured pathway from crisis to stability to permanent housing.

The Foundation's theory of change is grounded in evidence: stable housing is the prerequisite for sustained recovery from addiction, successful community reentry after incarceration, and long-term economic self-sufficiency. By deploying modular housing units in purpose-built Cornerstone Communities — paired with case management, peer mentorship, financial literacy, and down payment assistance — individuals progress through a structured pathway from crisis to stability to permanent housing. Each successful transition frees capacity for the next participant, creating a self-sustaining cycle of community impact.

---

## SECTION IV: ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY

### Leadership and Governance

FAITH Foundation is governed by a board of directors whose collective expertise in construction, financial management, housing industry practice, and community service directly supports the Foundation's mission and its capacity to manage federal funds responsibly.

**Reid Whitesides, Founder and President** brings more than 20 years of experience in construction, roofing, project management, sales, consulting, and housing-related industries. His commitment to this work is deeply personal: during a long struggle with addiction, Reid spent nearly twenty years incarcerated in the State of Texas, an experience that gave him firsthand insight into the barriers individuals face when rebuilding their lives after addiction, incarceration, and homelessness. Today, he has been sober for more than fifteen years. His lived experience, combined with his professional expertise, provides FAITH Foundation with a leader who understands both the urgency of this work and the practical mechanics of housing development, construction, and program management.

**Scott Ellis, Treasurer and Board Chair**, is the owner of E4 Roofing & Construction, a Georgetown, Texas-based company he has led for more than 15 years. Scott's experience in residential and commercial construction, project coordination, budgeting, contractor management, and building systems provides FAITH Foundation with directly applicable construction and housing industry expertise. His financial management experience as a business owner ensures that the Foundation approaches grant funds with the accountability and stewardship expected of federal fund recipients. His understanding of construction costs, building practices, and long-term asset stewardship ensures that Cornerstone Communities projects are executed responsibly and efficiently.

**Pastor Juan Valdez, Secretary and Protector**, brings nearly 30 years of ordained ministry experience and a lifetime of community leadership to the Foundation's governance structure. His 34-year history of successful business ownership in San Antonio — operating a hair studio at the same location for three decades — reflects the consistency, reliability, and stewardship that characterize his role in Foundation governance. Pastor Valdez provides spiritual oversight, governance accountability, and mission stewardship, ensuring that the Foundation remains faithful to its founding purpose and operates with integrity.

### Financial Management

FAITH Foundation maintains its financial records using QuickBooks and operates with an annual organizational budget of $75,000. The Foundation is committed to maintaining indirect costs below 15% of total program budget. Financial oversight is provided by Treasurer and Board Chair Scott Ellis, whose 15-year history of business ownership provides demonstrated capacity for financial stewardship and accountability. The Foundation's budget allocation prioritizes direct program delivery, with personnel costs supporting case managers maintaining a maximum 15-to-1 client ratio and a housing navigator who coordinates placement across transitional and permanent housing options.

FAITH Foundation is in its inaugural funding cycle, with initial operations funded through founder investment and church community support. The organization actively pursues diversified funding across government grants, private foundations, corporate giving programs, faith-based funders, and community development financial institutions to avoid dependency on any single source — a funding structure consistent with responsible management of federal CDBG funds.

### Program Infrastructure

FAITH Foundation's program infrastructure directly supports its capacity to manage and deliver results with CDBG funding:

- **Case Management System:** All program data is collected through FAITH Foundation's case management system, with quarterly reporting to the board of directors and annual impact reports published for all funders and stakeholders.
- **Partnership Network:** Active partnerships with recovery programs, reentry service providers, county social services agencies, local housing authorities, veterans service organizations, church partners, and building material suppliers ensure coordinated referral, wraparound services, and cost-effective program delivery.
- **Construction and Housing Expertise:** The combined construction expertise of Founder Reid Whitesides and Board Chair Scott Ellis — representing more than 35 combined years in housing-related construction, project management, and contractor management — ensures that modular unit acquisition and site development are executed with professional oversight and cost accountability.
- **Strategic Housing Partnership:** The Foundation's partnership with Bright Box Homes provides a direct pipeline to modular and manufactured housing units, enabling efficient deployment of acquired units at Cornerstone Communities sites.
- **In-Kind Contributions:** FAITH Foundation actively seeks and accepts in-kind donations of land, building materials, modular and manufactured housing units, construction equipment and labor, and professional services, significantly reducing cash outlays and stretching grant funding further. All in-kind contributions are documented at fair market value for matching fund compliance.

### Commitment to Rural Communities

FAITH Foundation's modular housing deployment model was specifically designed for rural communities. Units can be sited on donated or acquired rural land without the delays and costs of traditional construction, bringing housing solutions directly to underserved rural communities rather than concentrating resources in urban centers. Rural South Texas faces acute housing shortages with limited nonprofit infrastructure, and FAITH Foundation addresses this directly through a model that is practical, scalable, and deployable in communities that traditional affordable housing development has bypassed.

---

## SECTION V: INTENDED IMPACT AND EVALUATION

### Measurable Outcomes

FAITH Foundation measures impact across five interconnected domains, each corresponding to a priority population or program component funded under this request:

**Housing Placement:** Number of individuals and families transitioned from homelessness or unstable housing into transitional units and permanent housing, tracked by 30-, 60-, and 90-day retention rates.

**Financial Stability:** Number of down payment assistance awards disbursed, average award amount, and percentage of recipients maintaining stable housing at 12 months.

**Reentry Success:** Number of formerly incarcerated individuals housed, employment placement rates, and recidivism reduction compared to regional averages.

**Recovery Outcomes:** Number of individuals in active recovery housed through the program, sobriety milestones maintained, and connection rates to ongoing treatment and support services.

**Community Development:** Number of Cornerstone Communities sites developed, total modular housing units acquired and placed, occupancy rates, and successful transitions from transitional to permanent housing.

### Targets for CDBG-Funded Program Period

With CDBG funding support, FAITH Foundation is positioned to achieve the following outcomes during the grant period:

- Distribute down payment assistance awards to qualifying low-income families, with a target of 10 vouchers at $2,500 each totaling $25,000 in direct housing assistance
- Enroll 25 families in homeownership counseling and financial literacy programming as a prerequisite to down payment award eligibility
- Provide transitional housing placement to individuals exiting incarceration, addiction treatment, or housing crisis, with case management support through 90-day stability milestones
- Acquire modular housing units for deployment at Cornerstone Communities site(s) in rural South Texas, directly increasing affordable housing inventory available to CDBG priority populations
- Establish a minimum of 3 local employer partnerships for reentry and recovery program participants
- Achieve a 90% housing retention rate among assisted households at the 12-month interval

[NEEDS INPUT: Specific number of transitional housing beds or units to be funded with this grant award, and the specific rural Texas community or county where the funded Cornerstone Communities site will be located]

### Data Collection and Reporting

All program outcomes will be tracked through FAITH Foundation's case management system and reported to the funder on a quarterly basis consistent with CDBG reporting requirements. Annual impact reports will be published on the Foundation's website and made available to all funders. FAITH Foundation is committed to full transparency in financial stewardship and program outcomes, and will pursue third-party outcome verification beginning in Year 2 of operations.

---

## SECTION VI: SUSTAINABILITY

FAITH Foundation's long-term sustainability is built on a rotating housing asset model that ensures program capacity grows over time rather than depending on continuous capital infusion. As residents transition from Cornerstone Communities into permanent housing, their units become available for new participants, generating ongoing program capacity from existing assets.

Revenue streams supporting long-term operations include program fees assessed on a sliding scale based on participant income, rental income from stabilized housing units, recurring federal and state grant funding, corporate sponsorships and in-kind donations, church partnerships and congregational giving, and individual donor cultivation. The Foundation's partnership with Bright Box Homes — which donates $2,500 to FAITH Foundation for every home sold — provides a renewable, self-sustaining funding stream for the Down Payment Assistance Program that is not dependent on grant awards.

Physical assets — land parcels and modular housing units — appreciate over time and reduce ongoing capital expenditure requirements. The Foundation actively pursues diversified funding across government grants, private foundations, corporate giving programs, faith-based funders, and community development financial institutions to ensure no dependency on any single source. Operational costs are controlled through volunteer labor, donated building materials, and shared administrative infrastructure across program sites.

CDBG investment in FAITH Foundation's modular housing unit acquisition and transitional housing programming will generate durable, lasting community assets — physical housing units on acquired land — that continue to serve rural South Texas families for decades beyond the grant period.

---

## SECTION VII: BUDGET SUMMARY

[NEEDS INPUT: Specific line-item budget for the grant period, including the exact dollar amount requested within the $25,000–$150,000 range and allocation across program components (transitional housing, down payment assistance, modular unit acquisition, case management personnel, site preparation, etc.)]

FAITH Foundation's budget framework prioritizes direct program delivery over administrative overhead, with indirect costs maintained below 15% of total program budget. The following cost categories are applicable to this CDBG request:

**Personnel:** Case managers at a maximum 15-to-1 client ratio; housing navigator coordinating placement across transitional and permanent housing options; program administration.

**Capital — Modular Housing Unit Acquisition:** Modular and manufactured housing units at $30,000–$60,000 per unit, procured through the Foundation's partnership with Bright Box Homes.

**Capital — Site Preparation and Infrastructure:** Land preparation, utility infrastructure installation, and community common space construction at Cornerstone Communities sites.

**Direct Client Assistance:** Down payment assistance vouchers at $2,500 per household for qualifying low-income families.

**Operating Costs:** Property maintenance, insurance, participant support services, transportation for rural case management outreach, and program supplies.

**Indirect Costs:** Organizational administration, accounting (QuickBooks), grant reporting, compliance, and audit — maintained below 15% of total program budget.

In-kind contributions of building materials, volunteer construction labor, and professional services significantly reduce cash outlays and are documented at fair market value for matching fund purposes.

FAITH Foundation (Foundation for Affordable Instruction and Tenancy Hope)
EIN: 33, 2640449
Tax Status: 501(c)(3) Public Charity
Executive Director: Reid Whitesides
Geographic Service Area: South and Central Texas and the Texas Gulf Coast region, with primary focus on rural and underserved communities
Funding Request: [NEEDS INPUT: specific dollar amount requested within the $25,000–$150,000 range]

SECTION I: STATEMENT OF NEED

The Rural Texas Housing Crisis

Texas has one of the most severe affordable housing shortages in the country, and the weight of it falls hardest on the rural communities that get the least attention and the fewest resources. Nearly 28,000 Texans were experiencing homelessness during the 2024 Point, in, Time count, including 1,837 veterans. Forty, four percent of those individuals were entirely unsheltered, with no access to emergency shelter or transitional housing of any kind. Chronic homelessness in Texas climbed from 1,949 individuals in 2022 to 2,594 in 2023, a 33 percent increase in a single year. Meanwhile, the available supply of permanent supportive housing units reaches only 9.5 percent of those in need.

For rural South Texas, those numbers tell only part of the story.

Rural communities face acute housing shortages compounded by the near, total absence of nonprofit housing infrastructure. There are no large shelter systems here. No urban continuums of care with established capacity. No private rental markets capable of absorbing the demand. When a veteran exits service, when a man or woman completes addiction treatment, when a formerly incarcerated individual walks out of a Texas state prison, there is simply nowhere to go in many of the communities that need help most.

The Populations We Serve Face Compounded Barriers

The populations FAITH Foundation serves don't simply face housing scarcity. They face housing exclusion. Each population confronts a distinct but overlapping set of systemic barriers that make traditional affordable housing programs fall short.

Veterans experiencing housing insecurity represent 1,837 of the Texans counted as homeless in 2024. Texas ranks among the states with the highest concentrations of homeless veterans nationally. Many of these individuals carry service, connected disabilities, trauma histories, and disrupted employment records that make private market housing inaccessible regardless of available inventory.

Formerly incarcerated individuals face one of the most severe documented exclusions from the housing market of any population. Formerly incarcerated people are approximately 10 times more likely to experience homelessness than the general population. Between 23 and 48 percent of annual homeless shelter admissions nationally consist of formerly incarcerated individuals. Eighty, two percent of individuals released from prison across 24 states were re, arrested within 10 years of release, a recidivism cycle that stable housing directly interrupts. The absence of transitional housing options upon release isn't a contributing factor to reincarceration. It's a primary driver.

Individuals in addiction recovery face a window of maximum vulnerability during the transition out of treatment. Without stable housing, recovery collapses. Without recovery, stable housing stays out of reach. That compounding dynamic can't be broken with emergency shelter alone. It requires structured, supportive transitional housing in environments built specifically for recovery maintenance.

Single, parent families, the majority of them headed by single mothers, face a homeownership rate of approximately 34 percent, less than half the rate for married couples. Single, income households in rural Texas have no viable pathway to affordable housing without direct financial assistance and structured support.

Low, income families across all these populations face a down payment barrier that's grown to historic severity. The median age of a first, time homebuyer has risen to a record 40 years old. First, time buyers now represent just 21 percent of the market, the lowest share since the National Association of Realtors began tracking the metric in 1981. Seventy, four percent of homeowner households with incomes below $30,000 are cost, burdened, paying more than 30 percent of their income on housing. For the families FAITH Foundation serves, that burden is compounded by criminal records, gaps in employment history, limited savings, and the cascading effects of prior housing instability.

The Gap in Rural Texas

The national shortage of 7.3 million rental units affordable to extremely low, income households isn't distributed evenly. It concentrates in the places where construction is least profitable and infrastructure is least developed, rural communities like those FAITH Foundation serves across South and Central Texas. In these communities, there's insufficient housing inventory and insufficient financial assistance to bridge the gap between crisis and stability. Most existing programs address one side of this equation or the other. FAITH Foundation addresses both.

Stable housing is the prerequisite for sustained recovery from addiction, successful community reentry after incarceration, and long, term economic self, sufficiency. Without intervention at the transitional stage, before a veteran deteriorates back into unsheltered homelessness, before a returning citizen's release becomes a direct pathway to reincarceration, before a family in recovery loses its footing, the cycle continues at enormous cost to individuals, families, and the communities around them. FAITH Foundation exists to break that cycle at its root.

SECTION II: PROGRAM DESIGN

Overview

FAITH Foundation operates three interconnected housing programs in rural South and Central Texas, each designed to serve a specific stage of the pathway from crisis to permanent housing. These programs function as a coordinated continuum rather than isolated interventions, allowing participants to move through structured stages of stabilization at a pace appropriate to their individual circumstances.

Program 1: Down Payment Assistance Program

The Down Payment Assistance Program provides direct financial awards to qualifying low, income individuals and families to secure permanent housing. It targets specifically the people who've achieved employment stability but don't have the savings for upfront housing costs, the precise population for whom the growing down payment barrier has closed off homeownership. Priority goes to veterans, formerly incarcerated individuals, people in active recovery, and single, parent families. Awards bridge the gap between rental instability and permanent ownership, creating durable housing stability rather than temporary relief.

Program 2: Transitional Housing Program

The Transitional Housing Program places individuals exiting homelessness, incarceration, or addiction treatment into stable transitional units with case management support, financial literacy training, and peer mentorship for up to 24 months. Participants come in through referrals from recovery programs, reentry service partners, veterans service organizations, and county social services agencies. Case managers maintain a maximum 15, to, 1 client ratio to ensure meaningful, individualized support. Financial literacy programming prepares participants for the practical demands of independent housing, including budgeting, credit building, and debt management. Peer mentorship, provided through trained volunteers coordinated through faith community partners, reinforces recovery, accountability, and the relational stability that transitional housing alone can't supply.

Program 3: Cornerstone Communities Initiative

The Cornerstone Communities Initiative is FAITH Foundation's flagship capital development program and its most direct response to the supply, side failure driving rural Texas housing insecurity. The Foundation acquires land through purchase, donation, or below, market transfer and deploys modular and manufactured housing units to create purpose, built transitional micro, communities designed specifically for the populations we serve. Modular units, ranging from $30,000 to $60,000 per unit, can be sited on rural land without the delays and costs of traditional construction, bringing housing solutions directly to underserved rural communities rather than concentrating resources in urban centers.

Each Cornerstone Community includes individual housing units, shared community spaces, and on, site access to case management and support services including recovery programming and financial literacy education. Residents enter as transitional housing participants and progress toward permanent housing through FAITH Foundation's down payment assistance pipeline. As residents stabilize and transition out, their units become available for new participants, creating a self, sustaining cycle of community impact that doesn't require perpetual capital reinvestment to maintain capacity.

Theory of Change

Stable housing is the prerequisite for sustained recovery from addiction, successful community reentry after incarceration, and long, term economic self, sufficiency. FAITH Foundation's model addresses the root cause of cyclical homelessness, the absence of affordable transitional housing in rural communities. By deploying modular housing units in purpose, built Cornerstone Communities, paired with case management, peer mentorship, financial literacy, and down payment assistance, individuals progress through a structured pathway from crisis to stability to permanent housing. Each successful transition frees capacity for the next participant.

The model works because it doesn't treat symptoms in isolation. Emergency shelter without case management produces temporary relief. Down payment assistance without financial literacy produces unstable homeownership. Recovery housing without peer mentorship produces isolated sobriety. FAITH Foundation integrates all of these elements into a single, coordinated continuum in which each component reinforces the others and no participant moves to the next stage without the support structures in place to sustain it.

Target Population for This Funding Period

Funds awarded through this grant will directly serve veterans experiencing housing insecurity, individuals in addiction recovery transitioning out of treatment, formerly incarcerated individuals reentering their communities, single, parent families facing housing cost burden, and low, income individuals and families in rural South and Central Texas who lack access to down payment resources.

All participants must meet income eligibility requirements consistent with CDBG low, to, moderate income standards. [NEEDS INPUT: specific AMI thresholds applied for participant income eligibility]

Program Activities, Use of Grant Funds

Grant funds will be applied to the following direct program activities, consistent with CDBG, eligible uses and FAITH Foundation's verified program model.

Modular housing unit acquisition covers the purchase of modular and manufactured housing units for deployment at Cornerstone Communities development sites, with unit costs ranging from $30,000 to $60,000 depending on configuration and site requirements. Site preparation and utility infrastructure includes land clearing, foundation preparation, utility connection, and access improvements required to make acquired or donated parcels suitable for residential occupation. Down payment assistance awards are direct financial assistance disbursed to qualifying low, income individuals and families, with priority given to veterans, reentry participants, individuals in recovery, and single, parent families. Personnel costs support case managers maintaining a maximum 15, to, 1 client ratio and a housing navigator coordinating placement across transitional and permanent housing options. Transportation costs sustain case management coverage across geographically dispersed rural service areas where participants lack independent transportation. Community common space construction supports on, site programming, peer mentorship, and recovery support activities within Cornerstone Communities.

Participant Pathway and Program Design Elements

Participants are referred to FAITH Foundation through a network of community partners including recovery program providers, reentry service organizations, veterans service organizations, county social services agencies, and local housing authorities across South and Central Texas. Upon referral, a housing navigator assesses each participant and coordinates placement into the appropriate entry point, whether that's a transitional housing unit, down payment assistance, or emergency bridge housing, based on current stability level and housing goal.

During the transitional housing phase, participants receive individualized case management with a maximum 15, to, 1 staff, to, participant ratio. Financial literacy training equips them with practical budgeting, credit building, and debt management skills. Peer mentorship through trained church community volunteers provides relational support and accountability. As participants progress toward financial stability, the down payment assistance program provides the direct financial bridge to permanent housing.

The rural deployment model, using modular units sited on donated or acquired land, is specifically designed for the communities FAITH Foundation serves. Traditional construction is cost, prohibitive and slow in rural South Texas. Modular deployment brings quality, permanent housing to communities that would otherwise wait years or decades for conventionally financed affordable housing development.

SECTION III: ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY

Founding and Organizational History

FAITH Foundation was established by Reid Whitesides to address the critical shortage of affordable and transitional housing options in rural South Texas communities. The organization was founded on the conviction that stable housing is the essential foundation for recovery from addiction, successful reentry after incarceration, and long, term economic self, sufficiency. Drawing on the founder's background in construction, roofing, project management, and housing, related industries spanning more than 20 years, FAITH Foundation developed the Cornerstone Communities model as an approach to deploying affordable housing at scale in rural areas where traditional development is cost, prohibitive.

FAITH Foundation is a newly established organization in its inaugural funding cycle. Initial operations have been funded through founder investment and church community support. The organization is actively seeking its first institutional grant awards to launch formal program operations and initiate the first Cornerstone Communities development site.

Leadership Team

Reid Whitesides, Founder, President, and Executive Director

Reid Whitesides brings more than 20 years of experience in construction, roofing, project management, sales, consulting, and housing, related industries to his role leading FAITH Foundation. His commitment to the organization's mission is grounded in lived experience. During a long struggle with addiction, Reid spent nearly twenty years incarcerated in the State of Texas. He has been sober for more than fifteen years. That personal history gives him firsthand understanding of the barriers facing the populations FAITH Foundation serves, not as an abstraction, but as a daily reality he has navigated and overcome. Reid also develops websites, software applications, and automation tools in support of nonprofit and housing, focused initiatives. He leads the Foundation with the conviction that lives can be transformed when people are given access to hope, opportunity, and a stable foundation on which to build their future.

Scott Ellis, Treasurer and Board Chair

Scott Ellis is the owner of E4 Roofing and Construction, a Georgetown, Texas, based company he has led for more than 15 years. His experience as a business owner brings financial, operational, project management, and organizational expertise that applies directly to the Foundation's affordable housing development work. His background in residential and commercial construction, project coordination, budgeting, contractor management, and building systems means that Cornerstone Communities projects are approached with appropriate cost controls and construction discipline. A Georgetown, Texas resident for more than 24 years, Scott and his wife Christy are active members of their local church and have participated in mission work in Mexico. As Treasurer and Board Chair, Scott provides financial oversight and strategic leadership ensuring FAITH Foundation remains a faithful steward of its resources.

Pastor Juan Valdez, Secretary and Protector

Pastor Juan Valdez serves as Secretary and Protector of FAITH Foundation, providing spiritual oversight, governance accountability, and mission stewardship. With more than 40 years of Christian faith and nearly 30 years of ordained ministry experience, Pastor Valdez brings a lifetime of leadership grounded in integrity and service. His ministry has extended across the United States, South America, Central America, the Caribbean, and Africa. Beyond ministry, Pastor Valdez and his wife Martha operated a successful business in San Antonio for 34 years, a record of consistency, reliability, and stewardship that applies directly to organizational governance. He currently serves as an Associate Pastor at Temple of Praise and provides counsel on matters of governance, ethics, and mission alignment.

[NEEDS INPUT: names and qualifications of any additional board members not described in the Q&A]

Relevant Expertise and Capacity

The leadership team's combined background in construction and housing development, long, term organizational governance and community ministry, and direct lived experience with addiction, incarceration, and recovery gives FAITH Foundation a credible and operationally capable foundation for this work. That's not a common combination. Most organizations have one or two of those things. This team has all three.

Scott Ellis's ownership of a construction company with more than 15 years of operation provides direct capacity to oversee modular housing unit acquisition, site preparation, and Cornerstone Communities development, the precise capital activities for which these funds are being requested. That in, house construction expertise significantly reduces project management costs and risk compared to organizations procuring all construction oversight through third parties.

The organization's capacity to manage federal funds is supported by its established governance structure, board financial oversight through the Treasurer and Board Chair, and its commitment to maintaining indirect costs below 15 percent of total program budget. All financial records are maintained by the Treasurer and will be subject to independent audit as required by federal fund management standards. [NEEDS INPUT: name of accounting firm or financial management software used for fund tracking, if applicable]

Community Partnerships

FAITH Foundation maintains active partnerships across multiple sectors that directly expand the organization's reach and operational capacity.

Church partners provide volunteer labor, congregational fundraising, mentorship volunteers, and meeting space for participant programming. Recovery program partners refer individuals completing treatment who need stable transitional housing and provide ongoing support services for residents in active recovery. Reentry service partners coordinate placement of formerly incarcerated individuals into transitional housing upon release and connect them with employment services, legal aid, and family reunification support. County social services agencies and local housing authorities refer eligible families and individuals, coordinate benefits enrollment, and provide case management collaboration. Building material suppliers and modular housing manufacturers provide discounted or donated materials and units for Cornerstone Communities development. Land owners in rural South Texas donate or sell land at reduced cost for community development sites. Veterans service organizations refer military veterans experiencing housing insecurity and coordinate VA benefits enrollment.

FAITH Foundation also maintains a strategic partnership with Bright Box Homes, a container home builder that donates $2,500 to FAITH Foundation for every home sold, generating a recurring private, sector revenue stream for down payment assistance awards.

[NEEDS INPUT: specific named partner organizations willing to be listed or provide letters of support for this application]

Ability to Serve Rural Communities

FAITH Foundation's program model was designed specifically for the realities of rural South Texas. Modular housing unit deployment, the centerpiece of the Cornerstone Communities Initiative, enables the Foundation to site quality residential units on donated or acquired rural land without the permitting delays, contractor scarcity, and cost escalation that make traditional construction impractical in rural settings. Case management staff provide outreach coverage across geographically dispersed rural service areas using program vehicles. This model brings housing solutions directly to underserved rural communities rather than requiring participants to relocate to urban centers to access services.

SECTION IV: INTENDED IMPACT AND MEASURABLE OUTCOMES

Impact Framework

FAITH Foundation measures impact across five domains, tracked longitudinally with quarterly reporting and annual program evaluation.

Housing Placement tracks the number of individuals and families transitioned from homelessness or unstable housing into transitional units and permanent housing, measured by 30,  60,  and 90, day retention rates.

# Texas Community Development Block Grant – Housing
## Program Narrative

**Applicant Organization:** FAITH Foundation (Foundation for Affordable Instruction and Tenancy Hope)
**EIN:** 33-2640449
**Tax Status:** 501(c)(3) Public Charity
**Executive Director:** Reid Whitesides
**Geographic Service Area:** South and Central Texas and the Texas Gulf Coast region, with primary focus on rural and underserved communities
**Funding Request:** [NEEDS INPUT: specific dollar amount requested within the $25,000–$150,000 range]

---

## SECTION I: STATEMENT OF NEED

### The Rural Texas Housing Crisis

Texas is home to one of the most severe and persistent affordable housing shortages in the United States, and the burden falls most heavily on the rural communities that receive the least attention and the fewest resources. Nearly 28,000 Texans were experiencing homelessness during the 2024 Point-in-Time count, including 1,837 veterans. Forty-four percent of those individuals were entirely unsheltered — living without access to emergency shelter or transitional housing of any kind. Chronic homelessness in Texas increased from 1,949 individuals in 2022 to 2,594 in 2023, a 33 percent increase in a single year, while the available supply of permanent supportive housing units reaches only 9.5 percent of those in need.

For rural South Texas, these numbers tell only part of the story. Rural communities face acute housing shortages compounded by the near-total absence of nonprofit housing infrastructure. There are no large shelter systems, no urban continuums of care with established capacity, and no private rental markets capable of absorbing the demand. When a veteran exits service, when a man or woman completes addiction treatment, or when a formerly incarcerated individual is released from a Texas state prison, there is simply nowhere to go in many of the communities that need help most.

### The Populations We Serve Face Compounded Barriers

The populations FAITH Foundation serves do not simply face housing scarcity — they face housing exclusion. Each population confronts a distinct but overlapping set of systemic barriers that make traditional affordable housing programs inadequate.

**Veterans experiencing housing insecurity** represent 1,837 of the Texans counted as homeless in 2024. Texas ranks among the states with the highest concentrations of homeless veterans nationally. Many of these individuals carry service-connected disabilities, trauma histories, and disrupted employment records that make private market housing inaccessible regardless of available inventory.

**Formerly incarcerated individuals** face a documented exclusion from the housing market that is among the most severe of any population. Formerly incarcerated people are approximately 10 times more likely to experience homelessness than the general population. Between 23 and 48 percent of annual homeless shelter admissions nationally consist of formerly incarcerated individuals. Eighty-two percent of individuals released from prison across 24 states were re-arrested within 10 years of release — a recidivism cycle that stable housing directly interrupts. The absence of transitional housing options upon release is not a contributing factor to reincarceration; it is a primary driver.

**Individuals in addiction recovery** face a window of maximum vulnerability during the transition out of treatment. Without stable housing, recovery collapses. Without recovery, stable housing is unattainable. This compounding dynamic cannot be broken with emergency shelter alone. It requires structured, supportive transitional housing in environments designed specifically for recovery maintenance.

**Single-parent families**, the majority of them headed by single mothers, face a homeownership rate of approximately 34 percent — less than half the rate for married couples. Single-income households in rural Texas have no viable pathway to affordable housing without direct financial assistance and structured support.

**Low-income families across all populations** face a down payment barrier that has grown to historic severity. The median age of a first-time homebuyer has risen to a record 40 years old. First-time buyers now represent just 21 percent of the market, the lowest share since the National Association of Realtors began tracking the metric in 1981. Seventy-four percent of homeowner households with incomes below $30,000 are cost-burdened, paying more than 30 percent of their income on housing. For the families FAITH Foundation serves, this barrier is compounded by criminal records, gaps in employment history, limited savings, and the cascading effects of prior housing instability.

### The Gap in Rural Texas

The national shortage of 7.3 million rental units affordable to extremely low-income households is not distributed evenly. It concentrates in the places where construction is least profitable and infrastructure is least developed — rural communities like those FAITH Foundation serves across South and Central Texas. In these communities, there is insufficient housing inventory and insufficient financial assistance to bridge the gap between crisis and stability. Most existing programs address one side of this equation or the other. FAITH Foundation addresses both.

Stable housing is the prerequisite for sustained recovery from addiction, successful community reentry after incarceration, and long-term economic self-sufficiency. Without intervention at the transitional stage — before a veteran deteriorates back into unsheltered homelessness, before a returning citizen's release becomes a direct pathway to reincarceration, before a family in recovery loses its footing — the cycle continues at enormous cost to individuals, families, and the communities around them. FAITH Foundation exists to break that cycle at its root.

---

## SECTION II: PROGRAM DESIGN

### Overview

FAITH Foundation operates three interconnected housing programs in rural South and Central Texas, each designed to serve a specific stage of the pathway from crisis to permanent housing. These programs function as a coordinated continuum rather than isolated interventions, allowing participants to move through structured stages of stabilization at a pace appropriate to their individual circumstances.

**Program 1: Down Payment Assistance Program**
The Down Payment Assistance Program provides direct financial awards to qualifying low-income individuals and families to secure permanent housing. This program specifically targets individuals who have achieved employment stability but lack the savings required for upfront housing costs — the precise population for whom the growing down payment barrier has closed off homeownership. Priority is given to veterans, formerly incarcerated individuals, people in active recovery, and single-parent families. Awards bridge the gap between rental instability and permanent ownership, creating durable housing stability rather than temporary relief.

**Program 2: Transitional Housing Program**
The Transitional Housing Program places individuals exiting homelessness, incarceration, or addiction treatment into stable transitional units with accompanying case management support, financial literacy training, and peer mentorship for up to 24 months. Participants enter from referrals through recovery programs, reentry service partners, veterans service organizations, and county social services agencies. Case managers maintain a maximum 15-to-1 client ratio to ensure meaningful, individualized support. Financial literacy programming prepares participants for the practical demands of sustained independent housing, including budgeting, credit building, and debt management. Peer mentorship, provided through trained volunteers coordinated through faith community partners, reinforces recovery, accountability, and the relational stability that transitional housing alone cannot supply.

**Program 3: Cornerstone Communities Initiative**
The Cornerstone Communities Initiative is FAITH Foundation's flagship capital development program and its most direct response to the supply-side failure driving rural Texas housing insecurity. The Foundation acquires land through purchase, donation, or below-market transfer and deploys modular and manufactured housing units to create purpose-built transitional micro-communities designed specifically for the populations we serve. Modular housing units — ranging from $30,000 to $60,000 per unit — can be sited on rural land without the delays and costs of traditional construction, bringing housing solutions directly to underserved rural communities rather than concentrating resources in urban centers.

Each Cornerstone Community includes individual housing units, shared community spaces, and on-site access to case management and support services including recovery programming and financial literacy education. Residents enter as transitional housing participants and progress toward permanent housing through FAITH Foundation's down payment assistance pipeline. As residents stabilize and transition to permanent housing, their units become available for new participants — creating a self-sustaining cycle of community impact that does not require perpetual capital reinvestment to maintain capacity.

### Theory of Change

Stable housing is the prerequisite for sustained recovery from addiction, successful community reentry after incarceration, and long-term economic self-sufficiency. FAITH Foundation's model addresses the root cause of cyclical homelessness — the absence of affordable transitional housing in rural communities. By deploying modular housing units in purpose-built Cornerstone Communities, paired with case management, peer mentorship, financial literacy, and down payment assistance, individuals progress through a structured pathway from crisis to stability to permanent housing. Each successful transition frees capacity for the next participant, creating a self-sustaining cycle of community impact.

The model works because it does not treat symptoms in isolation. Emergency shelter without case management produces temporary relief. Down payment assistance without financial literacy produces unstable homeownership. Recovery housing without peer mentorship produces isolated sobriety. FAITH Foundation integrates all of these elements into a single, coordinated continuum in which each component reinforces the others and no participant is released into the next stage without the support structures in place to sustain it.

### Target Population for This Funding Period

Funds awarded through this grant will directly serve: veterans experiencing housing insecurity; individuals in addiction recovery transitioning out of treatment; formerly incarcerated individuals reentering their communities; single-parent families facing housing cost burden; and low-income individuals and families in rural South and Central Texas lacking access to down payment resources.

All participants must meet income eligibility requirements consistent with CDBG low-to-moderate income standards. [NEEDS INPUT: specific AMI thresholds applied for participant income eligibility]

### Program Activities — Use of Grant Funds

Grant funds awarded through this opportunity will be applied to the following direct program activities, consistent with CDBG-eligible uses and FAITH Foundation's verified program model:

- **Modular housing unit acquisition:** Purchase of modular and manufactured housing units for deployment at Cornerstone Communities development sites. Unit costs range from $30,000 to $60,000 per unit depending on configuration and site requirements.
- **Site preparation and utility infrastructure:** Land clearing, foundation preparation, utility connection, and access improvements required to make acquired or donated parcels suitable for residential occupation.
- **Down payment assistance awards:** Direct financial assistance disbursed to qualifying low-income individuals and families to secure permanent housing, with priority given to veterans, reentry participants, individuals in recovery, and single-parent families.
- **Case management and housing navigation:** Personnel costs for case managers maintaining a maximum 15-to-1 client ratio and a housing navigator coordinating placement across transitional and permanent housing options.
- **Transportation for rural outreach:** Program vehicles and transportation costs to sustain case management coverage across geographically dispersed rural service areas where participants lack independent transportation.
- **Community common space and program infrastructure:** Construction or installation of shared community spaces within Cornerstone Communities, supporting on-site programming, peer mentorship, and recovery support activities.

### Participant Pathway and Program Design Elements

Participants are referred to FAITH Foundation through a network of community partners including recovery program providers, reentry service organizations, veterans service organizations, county social services agencies, and local housing authorities across South and Central Texas. Upon referral, participants are assessed by a housing navigator who coordinates placement into the appropriate program entry point — transitional housing unit, down payment assistance, or emergency bridge housing — based on current stability level and housing goal.

During the transitional housing phase, participants receive individualized case management with a maximum 15-to-1 staff-to-participant ratio. Financial literacy training equips participants with practical budgeting, credit building, and debt management skills. Peer mentorship, provided through trained church community volunteers, offers relational support and accountability. As participants progress toward financial stability, the down payment assistance program provides the direct financial bridge to permanent housing.

The rural deployment model — using modular units sited on donated or acquired land — is specifically designed for the communities FAITH Foundation serves. Traditional construction is cost-prohibitive and slow in rural South Texas. Modular deployment brings quality, permanent housing to communities that would otherwise wait years or decades for conventionally financed affordable housing development.

Reid also develops websites, software applications, and automation tools in support of nonprofit and housing-focused initiatives. He leads the Foundation with a conviction that lives can be transformed when people are given access to hope, opportunity, and a stable foundation on which to build their future.

Scott Ellis is the owner of E4 Roofing & Construction, a Georgetown, Texas-based company he has led for more than 15 years.
