FAITH Foundation
Texas Community Development Block Grant – Housing
Program Narrative

SECTION I: ORGANIZATIONAL OVERVIEW

Legal Name: FAITH Foundation (Foundation for Affordable Instruction and Tenancy Hope)
EIN: 33, 2640449
Tax Status: 501(c)(3) Public Charity
Service Area: South and Central Texas, Texas Gulf Coast Region, with primary focus on rural and underserved communities
Annual Operating Budget: $75,000
Primary Contact: Reid Whitesides, Founder, President, and Executive Director

FAITH Foundation exists to break the cycle of housing insecurity by providing financial education, homeownership instruction, and direct housing assistance to veterans, individuals experiencing homelessness, single parents, those in recovery, those reentering society, and other economically disadvantaged populations. Through our Cornerstone Communities model and strategic partnership with Bright Box Homes, we turn charitable giving into permanent, affordable housing solutions.

Reid Whitesides founded this organization. He spent nearly two decades incarcerated in the State of Texas, has been sober for more than fifteen years, and brings more than twenty years of construction and housing industry experience to the work. FAITH Foundation is not a program administered from a comfortable distance. It's a mission built from what Reid lived, and the conviction that stable housing is the prerequisite for sustained recovery, successful reentry, and long, term self, sufficiency runs through everything we do.

We are a newly established organization in our inaugural funding cycle. Initial operations have been funded through founder investment and church community support. This application to the Texas Community Development Block Grant – Housing program represents our request to expand capacity to serve rural Texans who face the most acute and least, addressed housing needs in the state.

SECTION II: STATEMENT OF NEED

The Housing Crisis in Rural Texas

Texas is home to nearly 28,000 people experiencing homelessness, according to the 2024 HUD Point, in, Time Count, including 1,837 veterans. Forty, four percent of those individuals were unsheltered, meaning they had no access to emergency shelter or transitional housing of any kind. Chronic homelessness in Texas increased from 1,949 individuals in 2022 to 2,594 in 2023, a 33% increase in a single year.

Those numbers describe a statewide crisis. In rural South Texas, the primary geography this application addresses, the crisis is compounded by the near, total absence of nonprofit housing infrastructure. Urban centers attract the majority of housing, focused nonprofit resources, leaving rural communities with virtually no organized transitional housing capacity, no down payment assistance providers, and no affordable housing development pipeline.

The Populations at Greatest Risk

Texas has the second, highest concentration of homeless veterans in the nation. While veteran homelessness in Texas decreased 9.7% between 2023 and 2024, from 2,036 to 1,837, thousands of men and women who served their country remain without stable housing in this state. Rural veterans face compounding barriers: geographic isolation from VA services, limited public transportation, and a severe shortage of affordable housing units near where they want to rebuild their lives.

Formerly incarcerated individuals are approximately ten times more likely to experience homelessness than the general population. Research documents that between 23.1% and 47.8% of annual homeless shelter admissions nationally are formerly incarcerated individuals. Without stable housing, the path back to incarceration is short. People experiencing homelessness after release face increased law enforcement contact, supervision violations tied directly to their housing status, and far higher rates of reincarceration. FAITH Foundation's reentry housing model directly interrupts that cycle.

Stable housing is also the foundational prerequisite for sustained addiction recovery. Without it, the stressors, triggers, and social environments that drive relapse are simply unavoidable. Individuals completing addiction treatment in rural Texas routinely face a housing cliff. They exit treatment with nowhere stable to go. The absence of transitional housing in rural communities isn't a gap in the system. It's a gap that breaks the system.

Single, parent households tell a different version of the same story. The homeownership rate among single mothers is approximately 34%, compared to 84% for married couples without children. Single, parent households face home prices approaching five times their income. Down payment barriers, not income or desire, are the primary obstacle between a housing, insecure single parent and the stability that would secure their family's future.

The Supply Gap in Rural Communities

The national shortage of rental units affordable to extremely low, income households stands at 7.3 million. In rural South Texas, that shortage isn't theoretical. It's daily reality. Traditional affordable housing development is cost, prohibitive in rural areas: construction costs, contractor availability, infrastructure access, and population density make conventional multifamily development economically unviable for most developers. The communities with the greatest need receive the least investment.

FAITH Foundation's Cornerstone Communities model was designed specifically to solve this problem. Modular and manufactured housing units can be sited on donated or acquired rural land without the delays, costs, and density requirements of traditional construction. We bring housing solutions directly to underserved rural communities rather than waiting for market forces or urban, focused nonprofit infrastructure to reach them.

The Gap FAITH Foundation Fills

Most programs address either the demand side of the housing crisis, things like rental assistance, counseling, and emergency shelter, or the supply side through development. Rarely both. FAITH Foundation addresses both: direct down payment assistance and transitional housing placement on the demand side, land acquisition and modular housing unit deployment on the supply side. In rural South Texas, no comparable organization is providing this integrated model with a built, in sustainability mechanism. This application requests funding to activate and scale all three of FAITH Foundation's core programs in rural Texas communities.

SECTION III: PROGRAM DESIGN

Overview of FAITH Foundation's Three Core Programs

FAITH Foundation operates three interconnected housing programs, each targeting a distinct stage of the journey from housing crisis to permanent stability. All three prioritize military veterans, formerly incarcerated individuals, people in addiction recovery, single, parent families, and individuals experiencing or at risk of homelessness in rural and underserved South Texas communities.

Program 1: Down Payment Assistance Program

The Down Payment Assistance Program provides direct financial awards to qualifying low, income individuals and families to secure permanent housing. It targets people who are employment, stable but lack savings for upfront housing costs, the population for whom the down payment barrier, not income, is the primary obstacle to stability.

Awards are structured to bridge the gap between a participant's available savings and the upfront costs required to secure housing, whether a rental deposit that prevents homelessness or a down payment that enables homeownership. Award amounts [NEEDS INPUT: specific per, award dollar amount or range for this program cycle] are determined based on participant need and available funding. Before any award is disbursed, participants complete FAITH Foundation's financial literacy curriculum, ensuring that direct assistance is paired with the financial knowledge needed to sustain housing long, term.

Eligibility criteria include income at or below [NEEDS INPUT: AMI threshold, e.g., 80% of Area Median Income] of the area median income, demonstrated housing need, and participation in pre, disbursement counseling. Veterans, reentry individuals, and those in active recovery are prioritized throughout the selection process.

TXCDBG Alignment: This program directly addresses the funder's stated priority of down payment assistance for low, income families, with explicit priority populations matching TXCDBG's preference for reentry populations, individuals in recovery, and veterans experiencing housing insecurity.

Program 2: Transitional Housing Program

The Transitional Housing Program places individuals exiting homelessness, incarceration, or addiction treatment into stable transitional housing units with wraparound support services for up to 24 months. It addresses the housing cliff that is most acute in rural Texas: the moment when a person leaves incarceration, completes a treatment program, or exits an emergency shelter with nowhere stable to go.

Program components work together rather than in parallel. Transitional housing placement happens through FAITH Foundation's housing inventory and referral partnerships. Case management provides individualized goal planning, benefits enrollment assistance, and ongoing housing stability support. Financial literacy training covers budgeting, credit, building, debt management, and mortgage readiness. Peer mentorship pairs participants with people who have successfully navigated similar recovery or reentry experiences. Employment navigation connects participants to employment services and partner employers. Referral coordination links participants to recovery programs, legal aid, veterans service organizations, and family reunification services.

Participants receive transitional housing for up to 24 months, with case management intensity decreasing as stability increases. The program's goal isn't permanent transitional housing. It's transition to permanent housing. Case managers actively facilitate that progression throughout the program period, and down payment assistance is available for participants who reach the financial readiness threshold.

TXCDBG Alignment: This program directly addresses the funder's stated priority of transitional housing programs, with explicit design focus on reentry populations, individuals in recovery, and veterans.

Program 3: Cornerstone Communities Initiative

The Cornerstone Communities Initiative is FAITH Foundation's flagship housing development program and the supply, side answer to the rural Texas housing shortage. The Initiative acquires land in rural South Texas communities through purchase, donation, or reduced, cost sale, then deploys modular and manufactured housing units to create purpose, built transitional micro, communities designed specifically for the populations we serve.

Each Cornerstone Community includes individual housing units providing private, stable living space for transitional residents, shared community spaces for programming, peer support, case management, and community building, and on, site access to wraparound services including case management, recovery support, employment navigation, and financial literacy instruction.

Modular housing units are acquired at approximately $30,000 to $60,000 per unit, a fraction of the cost of traditional site, built construction. That cost efficiency matters enormously in rural markets where traditional development is economically unviable and where the people we serve are most concentrated and most underserved.

The Cornerstone Communities model is inherently self, sustaining. As residents stabilize and transition to permanent housing, their units become available for new participants. Physical assets, including land parcels and housing units, appreciate over time and reduce ongoing capital expenditure requirements for future program cycles.

Program Logic: From Crisis to Permanence

FAITH Foundation's three programs aren't independent initiatives. They're an integrated pathway. A veteran exiting the VA system or a formerly incarcerated individual released from a Texas state facility may enter through the Transitional Housing Program into a Cornerstone Community unit. Over 12 to 24 months, they participate in case management, financial literacy education, and peer mentorship. As they stabilize financially and professionally, they become eligible for Down Payment Assistance that transitions them into permanent housing. Their vacated unit then becomes available for the next participant.

This is not a shelter model. It is a pipeline to permanence.

SECTION IV: ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY

Leadership

FAITH Foundation is led by a founder with direct personal experience of the barriers this organization exists to remove, supported by a board with substantive construction, financial, and governance expertise.

Reid Whitesides, Founder, President, and Executive Director, brings more than twenty years of experience in construction, roofing, project management, sales, and housing, related industries. Veterans service organizations refer military veterans experiencing housing insecurity and coordinate VA benefits enrollment. Land owners in rural South Texas donate or sell land at reduced cost for community development sites.

These partnerships aren't aspirational. They're the operational infrastructure through which FAITH Foundation reduces costs, extends reach, and ensures that participants receive the full ecosystem of services they need to achieve lasting housing stability.

FAITH Foundation will track and report outcomes across five domains during the TXCDBG grant period.

Financial Stability: We will track the number of down payment assistance awards disbursed and the percentage of recipients maintaining stable housing at 12 months post, award.

Reentry Success: We will track the number of formerly incarcerated individuals housed through FAITH Foundation programs, employment placement rates among reentry participants, and recidivism rates compared to regional averages.

Recovery Outcomes: We will track the number of individuals in active recovery housed through Cornerstone Communities and the Transitional Housing Program, connection rates to ongoing treatment and support services, and sobriety milestone retention among housed participants.

Community Development: We will track the number of modular housing units acquired and placed, the number of Cornerstone Community sites developed or advanced during the grant period, and occupancy rates and successful transitions from transitional to permanent housing.

SECTION VII: SUSTAINABILITY

FAITH Foundation's long, term sustainability doesn't depend on any single funding source. We've designed our programs around a rotating housing asset model that generates ongoing capacity as residents transition to permanent housing and units become available for new participants.

Revenue streams include program participation fees assessed on a sliding scale based on participant income, rental income from stabilized housing units within the Cornerstone Communities portfolio, recurring grant funding from federal, state, and private foundation sources, and corporate sponsorships and in, kind donations. Church partnerships and congregational giving through our active church partner network, along with individual donor cultivation and recurring giving programs, round out the revenue picture.

Physical assets, land parcels and modular housing units, appreciate over time and reduce ongoing capital expenditure requirements. FAITH Foundation actively pursues diversified funding across government grants, private foundations, corporate giving programs, faith, based funders, and community development financial institutions to avoid dependency on any single source.

Each modular housing unit acquired and each land parcel secured becomes a permanent, appreciating community asset, one that generates program capacity, program revenue, and community impact for years beyond the initial grant period.

SECTION VIII: CONCLUSION

Rural South Texas communities face a housing crisis that is simultaneously acute and invisible. Invisible because the populations most affected are the least likely to be counted, heard, or served by traditional housing systems. Veterans who served their country and returned to rural communities with no support infrastructure. Men and women who completed addiction treatment and stepped out of the program door into homelessness. Formerly incarcerated Texans for whom the absence of stable housing isn't a personal failure but a predictable outcome of a system that releases people into nothing.

FAITH Foundation was built for exactly these communities and exactly these individuals. Our founder lived this experience. The Cornerstone Communities model was engineered for the rural context: low, cost, rapid, deployment, sustainable, and deeply rooted in the communities we serve. Our programs don't stop at emergency shelter. We provide the financial education, the case management, the transitional housing, and the down payment assistance needed to move people not just out of crisis, but into permanent, stable housing they can call their own.

We respectfully request Texas Community Development Block Grant – Housing funding to advance this mission. Every dollar invested in FAITH Foundation's programs creates a physical, permanent housing asset in a rural Texas community and a measurable, trackable pathway to stability for the veterans, reentry individuals, and recovery community members who need it most.

| **Total** | **[NEEDS INPUT]** | |

All funds will be expended in accordance with CDBG national objectives and applicable federal regulations. FAITH Foundation commits to maintaining complete documentation of all expenditures, participant eligibility determinations, and program outcomes for funder review and audit purposes.

---

## SECTION VI: INTENDED IMPACT AND OUTCOMES

### Measurable Outcomes for This Grant Period

FAITH Foundation will track and report outcomes across five domains during the TXCDBG grant period:

**1. Housing Placement**
- Number of individuals and families transitioned from homelessness or unstable housing into transitional units
- Number of participants transitioned from transitional housing to permanent housing
- Housing retention rates tracked at 30, 60, and 90 days, and at 6 and 12 months

**2. Financial Stability**
- Number of down payment assistance awards disbursed
- Percentage of recipients maintaining stable housing at 12 months post-award

**3. Reentry Success**
- Number of formerly incarcerated individuals housed through FAITH Foundation programs
- Employment placement rates among reentry participants
- Recidivism rates compared to regional averages

**4. Recovery Outcomes**
- Number of individuals in active recovery housed through Cornerstone Communities and the Transitional Housing Program
- Connection rates to ongoing treatment and support services
- Sobriety milestone retention among housed participants

**5. Community Development**
- Number of modular housing units acquired and placed
- Number of Cornerstone Community sites developed or advanced during the grant period
- Occupancy rates and successful transitions from transitional to permanent housing

### Specific Targets for This Funding Period

[NEEDS INPUT: Specific numerical targets for this grant period — e.g., number of participants served, number of units acquired, number of down payment awards disbursed — based on the specific dollar amount requested and program design for this cycle]

### Data Collection and Reporting

All program data will be collected through FAITH Foundation's case management system and reported on the schedule required by the funder. FAITH Foundation commits to full compliance with TXCDBG reporting requirements, including participant eligibility documentation, national objective compliance, and financial performance reporting. The Foundation's board of directors receives quarterly financial and program performance reports, ensuring ongoing governance oversight of all grant-funded activities.

---

## SECTION VII: SUSTAINABILITY

FAITH Foundation's long-term sustainability does not depend on any single funding source. The Foundation has designed its programs around a rotating housing asset model that generates ongoing capacity as residents transition to permanent housing and units become available for new participants.

Sustainability revenue streams include:

- **Program participation fees** assessed on a sliding scale based on participant income
- **Rental income** from stabilized housing units within the Cornerstone Communities portfolio
- **Recurring grant funding** from federal, state, and private foundation sources
- **Corporate sponsorships** and in-kind donations, including the Foundation's existing partnership with Bright Box Homes, which donates $2,500 to FAITH Foundation for every home sold — a renewable funding mechanism tied directly to new home construction activity
- **Church partnerships and congregational giving** through FAITH Foundation's active church partner network
- **Individual donor cultivation** and recurring giving programs

Physical assets — land parcels and modular housing units — appreciate over time and reduce ongoing capital expenditure requirements. FAITH Foundation actively pursues diversified funding across government grants, private foundations, corporate giving programs, faith-based funders, and community development financial institutions to avoid dependency on any single source.

TXCDBG funding for this program cycle will accelerate the Foundation's transition from a pre-asset to an asset-holding organization. Each modular housing unit acquired and each land parcel secured becomes a permanent, appreciating community asset — one that generates program capacity, program revenue, and community impact for years beyond the initial grant period.

---

## SECTION VIII: CONCLUSION

Rural South Texas communities face a housing crisis that is simultaneously acute and invisible — invisible because the populations most affected are the least likely to be counted, heard, or served by traditional housing systems. Veterans who served their country and returned to rural communities with no support infrastructure. Men and women who completed addiction treatment and stepped out of the program door into homelessness. Formerly incarcerated Texans for whom a lack of stable housing is not a personal failure but a predictable outcome of a system that releases people into nothing.

FAITH Foundation was built for exactly these communities and exactly these individuals. Our founder lived this experience. Our Cornerstone Communities model was engineered for the rural context — low-cost, rapid-deployment, sustainable, and deeply rooted in the communities we serve. Our programs do not stop at emergency shelter. We provide the financial education, the case management, the transitional housing, and the down payment assistance needed to move people not just out of crisis, but into permanent, stable housing they can call their own.

We respectfully request the Texas Community Development Block Grant – Housing funding to advance this mission. Every dollar invested in FAITH Foundation's programs creates a physical, permanent housing asset in a rural Texas community — and a measurable, trackable pathway to stability for the veterans, reentry individuals, and recovery community members who need it most.

SECTION I: ORGANIZATIONAL OVERVIEW

FAITH Foundation, the Foundation for Affordable Instruction and Tenancy Hope, is a Texas, based 501(c)(3) nonprofit built around a single conviction: that the populations most systematically shut out of stable housing deserve more than a waiting list. We serve military veterans, people in addiction recovery, formerly incarcerated individuals reentering society, single, parent families, and people experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Reid Whitesides founded this organization. He brings more than twenty years of experience in construction, roofing, and housing, and he also spent nearly two decades incarcerated in the State of Texas during a long struggle with addiction, and has now maintained his sobriety for more than fifteen years. FAITH Foundation doesn't describe these populations from a distance. It was built by someone who has walked that road and came back to build something for the people still on it.

The Foundation operates across South and Central Texas and the Texas Gulf Coast region, with a deliberate focus on rural and underserved communities where affordable transitional housing is scarcest and nonprofit infrastructure is thinnest. Our annual operating budget is $75,000, reflecting where we are in our founding year, and our governance team brings together construction industry expertise, ordained ministry leadership, and the kind of lived experience that no credential can replicate.

SECTION II: STATEMENT OF NEED

The Rural Texas Housing Crisis

Rural South Texas is facing a housing crisis that isn't one problem, it's three layered on top of each other: a shortage of affordable housing inventory, a near, total absence of transitional infrastructure for high, need populations, and the lack of a nonprofit ecosystem that urban centers have at least partially developed over decades. The numbers are unambiguous.

Nearly 28,000 Texans were experiencing homelessness as of the 2024 Point, in, Time count, including 1,837 veterans. Forty, four percent of those individuals were entirely unsheltered, meaning no emergency shelter, no transitional housing, nothing. Texas is one of six states that together account for 64% of the nation's total homeless population. And within Texas, the weight of that crisis falls hardest on the communities least equipped to carry it.

The populations FAITH Foundation serves face barriers that multiply the general homeless population's challenges many times over. Formerly incarcerated individuals are approximately ten times more likely to experience homelessness than the general population. Research across multiple states documents that between 23% and 48% of annual homeless shelter admissions are individuals recently released from incarceration. Stable housing after release isn't a quality, of, life nicety. It is the single most reliable predictor of successful reentry. People released into homelessness face dramatically elevated risks of supervision violations, law enforcement contact, and reincarceration, not because of criminal inclination, but because housing instability itself generates the conditions for reincarceration. The nation faces a shortage of 7.3 million rental units affordable to extremely low, income households, and individuals with criminal records are already excluded from most private market options, compressing their already, narrow choices further.

Veterans face a parallel crisis. Texas has among the highest concentrations of homeless veterans of any state, with 1,837 identified in the 2024 Point, in, Time count, a figure that understates reality given the well, documented undercounting of rural and unsheltered veterans. Texas veteran homelessness did decrease 9.7% between 2023 and 2024, which tells us targeted intervention works. But tens of thousands of people who served this country still don't have stable housing in the state they call home.

For people in addiction recovery, the absence of stable transitional housing is one of the most common and consequential relapse triggers there is. Completing a treatment program and returning to the same unstable environment, or to no environment at all, dismantles the gains made in treatment faster than almost anything else. Rural South Texas has limited sober living infrastructure and virtually no purpose, built transitional housing designed for this population.

The down payment barrier compounds everything for families trying to move from instability to permanent homeownership. First, time homebuyers now represent just 21% of the market, the lowest share since tracking began in 1981. The median age of a first, time homebuyer has climbed to a record 40 years old. For the people we serve, that barrier isn't primarily about credit or income alone. It's about the impossibility of accumulating savings while simultaneously navigating housing instability, recovery, or reentry. Direct down payment assistance, targeted to employment, stable individuals who've crossed the threshold of crisis but can't bridge the gap to ownership, addresses a genuine and documented market failure.

Why Rural Communities Are Underserved

Rural South Texas doesn't have the density of nonprofit housing infrastructure that exists in urban centers. Emergency shelters, transitional housing programs, sober living facilities, and reentry housing providers are concentrated in San Antonio, Houston, Austin, and the urban cores of the Rio Grande Valley. Someone returning to a rural community after incarceration, or completing treatment in a rural setting, finds almost nothing waiting for them. Traditional affordable housing development is cost, prohibitive in rural markets where development economics, contractor availability, and infrastructure costs combine to make conventional construction impractical for a small nonprofit. That gap is exactly what FAITH Foundation's modular housing model is designed to fill.

SECTION III: PROGRAM DESIGN

Program Overview

FAITH Foundation operates three interconnected housing programs that together address both the immediate crisis of housing instability and the structural barriers to permanent housing for the populations this grant opportunity prioritizes.

Program 1: Down Payment Assistance Program

The Down Payment Assistance Program provides direct financial awards to qualifying low, income individuals and families to secure permanent housing. We're not targeting people in acute crisis here. This program is for people who have already crossed that threshold, who are employment, stable and engaged in recovery or reentry programming, but who can't accumulate savings for upfront housing costs because of the cumulative financial effects of incarceration, addiction, or chronic housing instability.

Awards are structured to bridge the gap between rental instability and ownership or stable long, term tenancy, so participants can secure permanent housing without cycling back into transitional dependence. Eligibility prioritizes the populations identified in this funding opportunity: veterans experiencing housing insecurity, individuals in recovery from addiction, formerly incarcerated individuals reentering society, single, parent families, and other low, income households in rural South Texas communities.

Funds requested through this grant opportunity would be deployed as direct down payment assistance awards, with award amounts of [NEEDS INPUT: specific down payment award amount per recipient to be confirmed based on final budget allocation] per qualifying household.

Program 2: Transitional Housing Program

The Transitional Housing Program places individuals exiting homelessness, incarceration, or addiction treatment into stable transitional units for up to 24 months, with case management support, financial literacy training, and peer mentorship throughout. This program directly serves the reentry, recovery, and veteran populations identified as priority populations for this funding opportunity.

Participants receive structured support across the full arc of their transition: immediate stable shelter first, then ongoing case management, connection to employment services and benefits enrollment, financial literacy education, and peer mentorship from individuals who've successfully completed the program. The 24, month window isn't arbitrary. It reflects a clear, eyed recognition that stable reentry and sustained recovery require durable support structures, not 30, or 90, day emergency placements that return people to instability before they've built the capacity to hold housing on their own.

Program 3: Cornerstone Communities Initiative

The Cornerstone Communities Initiative is FAITH Foundation's flagship housing development program and the vehicle through which this grant's acquisition and development funding will be deployed. We acquire land through purchase, donation, or partnership with landowners willing to sell at reduced cost, then deploy modular and manufactured housing units to create purpose, built transitional micro, communities designed specifically for the people we serve.

Each Cornerstone Community is designed as a complete transitional environment: individual housing units that provide private, dignified shelter, shared community spaces that support peer connection and programming, and on, site access to case management and wraparound support services. The micro, community model isn't incidental to the program design. It is the program design. People rebuilding their lives after incarceration, in active recovery, or transitioning out of homelessness need more than four walls. They benefit from a community of peers navigating the same journey, supported by staff and volunteers who have often walked that road themselves.

The modular deployment model is specifically suited to rural South Texas conditions. Modular and manufactured housing units can be sited on acquired or donated rural land without the delays, contractor availability problems, and per, unit costs of traditional site, built construction. We bring housing solutions into rural communities rather than requiring rural residents to relocate to urban centers to access services, a displacement that severs the employment connections, family ties, and community support networks that are often critical to recovery and reentry success.

As residents stabilize and transition to permanent housing, their units open up for new participants. That rotating model isn't theoretical. It's the structural mechanism by which a single capital investment in housing units generates ongoing community impact without requiring continuous capital reinvestment at the same scale.

Population Served

FAITH Foundation's programs serve veterans experiencing housing insecurity, including those navigating the transition from military service to civilian housing, veterans in recovery or reentry, and veterans who have experienced chronic homelessness. We serve individuals in active addiction recovery who are completing residential treatment programs and need stable transitional housing to sustain what they've worked for. We serve formerly incarcerated individuals reentering society, with particular attention to those returning to rural South Texas communities where reentry housing resources are most scarce. We serve single, parent families facing housing cost burden without dual, income capacity. And we serve low, income individuals and families meeting income eligibility thresholds appropriate for CDBG, funded housing assistance in rural Texas communities.

Theory of Change

Stable housing is the prerequisite for everything else. Sustained recovery. Successful reentry. Long, term economic self, sufficiency. You can't build any of those things without a foundation, and FAITH Foundation's model addresses the root cause of cyclical homelessness in rural communities: the absence of affordable transitional housing and the absence of a structured pathway from crisis to stability to permanent housing.

By deploying modular housing units in purpose, built Cornerstone Communities, paired with case management, peer mentorship, financial literacy education, and direct down payment assistance, individuals move through a structured pathway from crisis to stability to permanent housing. Each successful transition frees capacity for the next participant. The result isn't a static service. It's a self, sustaining cycle of community impact in which early capital investment generates ongoing housing capacity for the populations who need it most.

Program Activities and Use of Requested Funds

Funds awarded through this grant opportunity will be deployed across four activities, all directly aligned with the funding categories identified in this opportunity.

Acquisition of modular housing units for Cornerstone Communities development aligns with the funder's priority of affordable housing development and modular unit acquisition. [NEEDS INPUT: specific site/land parcel details if available] site preparation and utility infrastructure aligns with affordable housing development in rural Texas communities. Down payment assistance awards to qualifying low, income veterans, reentry, and recovery participants aligns with the funder's down payment assistance priority for low, income families and reentry and recovery populations. Transitional housing placement and case management for program participants aligns with transitional housing programs for reentry, recovery, and veteran populations.

[NEEDS INPUT: Specific budget line items with exact dollar amounts broken down by category, including modular unit acquisition cost, site preparation cost, down payment assistance pool, and case management operational costs, are required to complete the budget narrative.]

SECTION IV: ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY

Leadership and Governance

FAITH Foundation's leadership team brings the specific expertise this work demands: construction and housing industry knowledge, financial oversight and business management, ministry and governance experience, and the lived experience of the populations the Foundation serves.

Reid Whitesides, Founder, President, and Executive Director, brings more than twenty years of experience in construction, roofing, project management, sales, and housing, related industries. His commitment to this mission is grounded in something no resume captures: Reid spent nearly twenty years incarcerated in the State of Texas during a long struggle with addiction, and has maintained his sobriety for more than fifteen years. He leads FAITH Foundation with the direct understanding of what is at stake for the individuals we serve, not as an abstraction, but as someone who has navigated the exact barriers the Foundation exists to dismantle.

Scott Ellis, Treasurer and Board Chair, is the owner of E4 Roofing and Construction in Georgetown, Texas, which he has led for more than fifteen years. Scott brings practical construction and housing industry expertise directly applicable to the Foundation's housing development activities, including residential and commercial construction, project coordination, budgeting, contractor management, and long, term asset stewardship. His financial oversight role ensures responsible stewardship of grant funds and accountability for project, level budgets. Scott and his wife Christy are active members of their local church and have been Georgetown residents for more than twenty, four years.

Pastor Juan Valdez, Secretary, brings more than forty years of Christian faith and nearly thirty years of ordained ministry experience to the Foundation's governance. He currently serves as Associate Pastor at Temple of Praise in Texas. He and his wife Martha operated a successful business in San Antonio for thirty, four years, which is its own kind of testimony to the consistency and reliability of stewardship that characterizes his governance role. Pastor Valdez provides spiritual oversight, governance accountability, and mission stewardship for the organization.

Relevant Experience and Program Track Record

FAITH Foundation is in its inaugural funding cycle, with initial operations funded through founder investment and church community support. The organization was established specifically to address critical gaps in rural South Texas housing infrastructure that existing providers aren't filling.

The Foundation's capacity to manage and deploy housing, focused federal funds is grounded in several areas. Construction and project management expertise at the board and executive level includes demonstrated experience managing residential construction projects, contractor relationships, and building system budgets directly applicable to modular housing acquisition and site development. Housing industry knowledge spans the full development lifecycle, from site identification and acquisition through construction management and long, term asset stewardship. Program design is aligned with evidence, based models documented by HUD, the VA, and peer organizations operating transitional housing, reentry housing, and down payment assistance programs. And active partnerships with local churches, recovery programs, reentry service providers, county social services agencies, housing authorities, building material suppliers, modular housing manufacturers, and landowners across South Texas provide the referral, service coordination, and development networks necessary to operate at scale.

Partnerships

FAITH Foundation maintains active partnerships across multiple sectors that directly support program delivery and housing development. Church partners provide volunteer labor, congregational fundraising, mentorship volunteers, and meeting space for participant programming. Recovery program partners refer individuals completing treatment who need stable transitional housing and provide ongoing support services for residents in active recovery. Reentry service partners coordinate placement of formerly incarcerated individuals into transitional housing upon release and connect participants to employment services, legal aid, and family reunification support. County social services agencies and local housing authorities refer eligible families, coordinate benefits enrollment, and provide case management collaboration. Building material suppliers and modular housing manufacturers provide discounted or donated materials and units for Cornerstone Communities development. Rural landowners donate or sell land at reduced cost for community development sites. Veterans service organizations refer military veterans experiencing housing insecurity and coordinate VA benefits enrollment.

[NEEDS INPUT: Specific named partner organizations, if any formal partnership agreements or letters of support are available, should be listed here to strengthen capacity documentation.]

Financial Management Capacity

FAITH Foundation's annual operating budget is $75,000. The Foundation maintains the financial management systems, board, level financial oversight, and operational infrastructure appropriate to its current stage of operations.

[NEEDS INPUT: Information about the organization's accounting systems, financial controls, and any prior experience managing federal or state grant funds, including whether a financial audit, review, or compilation has been conducted, is needed to complete the federal funds management capacity documentation required by CDBG eligibility standards.]

Sustainability

FAITH Foundation's long, term sustainability is built on a rotating housing asset model that generates ongoing capacity without requiring continuous capital reinvestment at the same scale. As Cornerstone Communities residents transition to permanent housing, units open up for new participants, compounding the impact of initial capital investment over time.

Revenue streams supporting organizational sustainability include program fees assessed on a sliding scale based on participant income, rental income from stabilized housing units, recurring grant funding from federal, state, and private sources, corporate sponsorships and in, kind donations, church partnerships and congregational giving, and individual donor cultivation. Physical assets, land parcels and modular housing units, appreciate over time and reduce ongoing capital expenditure requirements. Operational costs are controlled through volunteer labor, donated materials, and shared administrative infrastructure across program sites.

The Foundation actively pursues diversified funding across government grants, private foundations, corporate giving programs, faith, based funders, and community development financial institutions. We don't want to be dependent on any single source. Funds awarded through this grant opportunity will be deployed as permanent housing assets, modular units and land, that generate ongoing program capacity independent of future grant cycles.

SECTION V: INTENDED IMPACT AND MEASUREMENT

Projected Outcomes

FAITH Foundation will measure program impact across five domains, with outcomes tracked longitudinally and reported quarterly.

On housing placement, we track the number of individuals and families transitioned from homelessness or unstable housing into transitional Cornerstone Communities units, the number of program participants transitioned from transitional housing to permanent housing, and 30,  60,  and 90, day housing retention rates for transitional program participants.

On financial stability, we track the number of down payment assistance awards disbursed and the total dollar value of those awards, along with the percentage of down payment assistance recipients maintaining stable housing at 12 months post, award.

On reentry success, we track the number of formerly incarcerated individuals housed through Transitional Housing and Cornerstone Communities programs, employment placement rates among reentry participants within 90 days of program enrollment, and recidivism rates compared to regional baselines for reentry participants at 24 months.

On recovery outcomes, we track the number of individuals in active recovery housed through the program, sobriety milestone maintenance rates among recovery housing participants, and connection rates to ongoing treatment and peer support services.

On community development, we track the number of Cornerstone Communities sites developed or expanded with grant funds, total modular housing units acquired and placed, and occupancy rates and successful transitions from transitional to permanent housing per unit per year.

[NEEDS INPUT: Year 1 numeric targets for participants served under this specific grant, funded program, including number of households receiving down payment assistance, number of transitional housing units acquired, and number of individuals housed, are required to complete this section. Targets should be proportionate to the requested grant amount and realistic given the organization's current stage of operations.]

Data Collection and Reporting

All program data will be collected through FAITH Foundation's case management system and reported quarterly to the board of directors and, as required, to the funding agency. We're committed to transparency in financial stewardship and program outcomes. The Foundation will maintain records of all grant expenditures, participant enrollment and outcomes, and housing asset deployment in compliance with CDBG reporting requirements.

SECTION VI: ALIGNMENT WITH FUNDER PRIORITIES

This application directly addresses every priority identified in the Texas Community Development Block Grant Housing funding opportunity.

On affordable housing development, the Cornerstone Communities Initiative deploys modular housing acquisition and site development in rural South Texas. On transitional housing programs, the Transitional Housing Program provides up to 24, month placements with case management for reentry, recovery, and veteran populations. On down payment assistance for low, income families, the Down Payment Assistance Program provides direct awards to employment, stable low, income individuals and families. On acquisition of modular housing units in rural Texas communities, the Cornerstone Communities Initiative creates purpose, built modular micro, communities on acquired or donated rural land. On reentry populations, a dedicated transitional housing and case management program component serves formerly incarcerated individuals. On individuals in recovery, a structured transitional housing continuum serves individuals in active recovery from addiction. On veterans experiencing housing insecurity, a dedicated program component provides housing assistance, VA benefits navigation, and case management for veterans. On rural Texas communities, the Foundation's explicit geographic focus on rural South and Central Texas is matched by a modular deployment model specifically designed for rural development economics.

FAITH Foundation isn't a general social services organization that identified housing as an adjacent funding opportunity. It was built, from day one, to address the precise intersection of rural affordable housing development, transitional housing for reentry and recovery populations, and veteran housing insecurity that this funding opportunity prioritizes. The founder's lived experience of incarceration, addiction, and recovery informs every program design decision the organization has made. The board's construction and housing industry expertise ensures that capital investments in modular housing acquisition and site development are managed with the accountability and competence that federal community development funding requires.

REQUIRED ATTACHMENTS

The following documents are submitted with this application: IRS 501(c)(3) Determination Letter (EIN: 33, 2640449), Organizational Budget for the current fiscal year, Board of Directors List, Program Narrative (this document), and Budget Narrative.

[NEEDS INPUT: Budget narrative with specific line, item costs broken down by program activity, including per, unit modular housing acquisition cost, site preparation cost per unit and site, down payment assistance award amounts and number of awards, and case management operational costs, must be completed before submission. Final requested grant amount within the $25,000 to $150,000 range must also be confirmed.]

For questions regarding this application, contact:
Reid Whitesides, Executive Director, FAITH Foundation

---

## SECTION III: PROGRAM DESIGN

### Program Overview

The 24-month program window reflects an evidence-informed recognition that stable reentry and sustained recovery require durable support structures, not 30- or 90-day emergency placements that return individuals to instability before they have achieved the stability necessary to maintain housing independently.

#### Program 3: Cornerstone Communities Initiative

The Cornerstone Communities Initiative is FAITH Foundation's flagship housing development program and the vehicle through which this grant's acquisition and development funding will be deployed. The Initiative acquires land — through purchase, donation, or partnership with landowners willing to sell at reduced cost — and deploys modular and manufactured housing units to create purpose-built transitional micro-communities designed specifically for the populations the Foundation serves.

Each Cornerstone Community is designed as a complete transitional environment: individual housing units providing private, dignified shelter; shared community spaces supporting peer connection and programming; and on-site access to case management and wraparound support services. The micro-community model is not incidental to the program design — it is the program design. Individuals rebuilding their lives after incarceration, in active recovery, or transitioning out of homelessness benefit not only from stable shelter but from a community of peers navigating the same journey, supported by staff and volunteers who have often walked that road themselves.

The modular housing deployment model is specifically suited to rural South Texas conditions. Modular and manufactured housing units can be sited on acquired or donated rural land without the delays, contractor availability challenges, and per-unit costs of traditional site-built construction. This approach brings housing solutions directly into rural communities rather than requiring rural residents to relocate to urban centers to access services — a displacement that severs employment connections, family ties, and community support networks that are often critical to recovery and reentry success.

As residents stabilize and transition to permanent housing, their units become available for new participants, creating a self-sustaining cycle of housing capacity. The rotating model is not theoretical — it is the structural mechanism by which a single capital investment in housing units generates ongoing community impact without requiring continuous capital re-investment at the same scale.

### Population Served

FAITH Foundation's programs serve the following populations, all of which align directly with the priority populations identified in this funding opportunity:

- **Veterans experiencing housing insecurity**, including those navigating the transition from military service to civilian housing, veterans in recovery or reentry, and veterans who have experienced chronic homelessness
- **Individuals in addiction recovery**, including those completing residential treatment programs who need stable transitional housing to sustain their recovery outside of a treatment environment
- **Formerly incarcerated individuals reentering society**, with particular attention to individuals returning to rural South Texas communities where reentry housing resources are most scarce
- **Single-parent families** facing housing cost burden and lacking the dual-income capacity of two-parent households
- **Low-income individuals and families** meeting income eligibility thresholds appropriate for CDBG-funded housing assistance in rural Texas communities

### Theory of Change

Stable housing is the prerequisite for sustained recovery from addiction, successful community reentry after incarceration, and long-term economic self-sufficiency. FAITH Foundation's model addresses the root cause of cyclical homelessness in rural communities: the absence of affordable transitional housing options and the absence of a structured pathway from crisis to stability to permanent housing.

By deploying modular housing units in purpose-built Cornerstone Communities, paired with case management, peer mentorship, financial literacy education, and direct down payment assistance, individuals progress through a structured pathway from crisis to stability to permanent housing. Each successful transition frees capacity for the next participant. The result is not a static service — it is a self-sustaining cycle of community impact in which early capital investment generates ongoing housing capacity for the populations who need it most.

### Program Activities and Use of Requested Funds

Funds awarded through this grant opportunity will be deployed across the following activities, all directly aligned with the funding categories identified in this opportunity:

| Activity | Alignment with Funder Priorities |
|---|---|
| Acquisition of modular housing units for Cornerstone Communities development | Acquisition of modular housing units; affordable housing development |
| [NEEDS INPUT: specific site/land parcel details if available] site preparation and utility infrastructure | Affordable housing development in rural Texas communities |
| Down payment assistance awards to qualifying low-income veterans, reentry, and recovery participants | Down payment assistance for low-income families; reentry and recovery populations |
| Transitional housing placement and case management for program participants | Transitional housing programs; reentry, recovery, and veteran populations |

[NEEDS INPUT: Specific budget line items with exact dollar amounts broken down by category — modular unit acquisition cost, site preparation cost, down payment assistance pool, and case management operational costs — are required to complete the budget narrative.]

---

## SECTION IV: ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY

### Leadership and Governance

FAITH Foundation's leadership team combines the specific expertise this work demands: construction and housing industry knowledge, financial oversight and business management, ministry and governance experience, and the lived experience of the populations the Foundation serves.

**Reid Whitesides, Founder, President, and Executive Director**, brings more than twenty years of experience in construction, roofing, project management, sales, and housing-related industries. His commitment to this mission is grounded in personal experience: Reid spent nearly twenty years incarcerated in the State of Texas during a long struggle with addiction, and has maintained sobriety for more than fifteen years. He leads FAITH Foundation with the direct understanding of what is at stake for the individuals the organization serves — not as an abstraction, but as someone who has navigated the barriers the Foundation exists to dismantle.

**Scott Ellis, Treasurer and Board Chair**, is the owner of E4 Roofing & Construction in Georgetown, Texas, which he has led for more than fifteen years. Scott brings practical construction and housing industry expertise directly applicable to the Foundation's housing development activities: residential and commercial construction, project coordination, budgeting, contractor management, and long-term asset stewardship. His financial oversight role ensures responsible stewardship of grant funds and accountability for project-level budgets. Scott and his wife, Christy, are active members of their local church and have been Georgetown residents for more than twenty-four years.

**Pastor Juan Valdez, Secretary**, brings more than forty years of Christian faith and nearly thirty years of ordained ministry experience to the Foundation's governance. He currently serves as Associate Pastor at Temple of Praise in Texas. He and his wife, Martha, operated a successful business in San Antonio for thirty-four years — demonstrating the consistency and reliability of stewardship that characterizes his governance role. Pastor Valdez provides spiritual oversight, governance accountability, and mission stewardship for the organization.

### Relevant Experience and Program Track Record

FAITH Foundation is in its inaugural funding cycle, with initial operations funded through founder investment and church community support. The organization was established specifically to address critical gaps in rural South Texas housing infrastructure that existing providers are not filling.

The Foundation's capacity to manage and deploy housing-focused federal funds is grounded in:

- **Construction and project management expertise** at the board and executive level, including demonstrated experience managing residential construction projects, contractor relationships, and building system budgets directly applicable to modular housing acquisition and site development
- **Housing industry knowledge** spanning the full development lifecycle, from site identification and acquisition through construction management and long-term asset stewardship
- **Program design aligned with evidence-based models** documented by HUD, the VA, and peer organizations operating transitional housing, reentry housing, and down payment assistance programs
- **Active partnerships** with local churches, recovery programs, reentry service providers, county social services agencies, housing authorities, building material suppliers, modular housing manufacturers, and landowners across South Texas — the referral, service coordination, and development networks necessary to operate at scale

### Partnerships

FAITH Foundation maintains active partnerships across multiple sectors that directly support program delivery and housing development:

- **Church partners** provide volunteer labor, congregational fundraising, mentorship volunteers, and meeting space for participant programming
- **Recovery program partners** refer individuals completing treatment who need stable transitional housing and provide ongoing support services for residents in active recovery
- **Reentry service partners** coordinate placement of formerly incarcerated individuals into transitional housing upon release and connect participants to employment services, legal aid, and family reunification support
- **County social services agencies and local housing authorities** refer eligible families, coordinate benefits enrollment, and provide case management collaboration
- **Building material suppliers and modular housing manufacturers** provide discounted or donated materials and units for Cornerstone Communities development
- **Rural landowners** donate or sell land at reduced cost for community development sites
- **Veterans service organizations** refer military veterans experiencing housing insecurity and coordinate VA benefits enrollment

[NEEDS INPUT: Specific named partner organizations, if any formal partnership agreements or letters of support are available, should be listed here to strengthen capacity documentation.]

### Financial Management Capacity

FAITH Foundation's annual operating budget is $75,000. The Foundation maintains the financial management systems, board-level financial oversight, and operational infrastructure appropriate to its current stage of operations.

[NEEDS INPUT: Information about the organization's accounting systems, financial controls, and any prior experience managing federal or state grant funds — including whether a financial audit, review, or compilation has been conducted — is needed to complete the federal funds management capacity documentation required by CDBG eligibility standards.]

### Sustainability

FAITH Foundation's long-term sustainability is built on a rotating housing asset model that generates ongoing capacity without requiring continuous capital reinvestment at the same scale. As Cornerstone Communities residents transition to permanent housing, units become available for new participants, compounding the impact of initial capital investment over time.

Revenue streams supporting organizational sustainability include program fees assessed on a sliding scale based on participant income, rental income from stabilized housing units, recurring grant funding from federal, state, and private sources, corporate sponsorships and in-kind donations, church partnerships and congregational giving, and individual donor cultivation. Physical assets — land parcels and modular housing units — appreciate over time and reduce ongoing capital expenditure requirements. Operational costs are controlled through volunteer labor, donated materials, and shared administrative infrastructure across program sites.

The Foundation actively pursues diversified funding across government grants, private foundations, corporate giving programs, faith-based funders, and community development financial institutions to avoid dependency on any single source. Funds awarded through this grant opportunity will be deployed as permanent housing assets — modular units and land — that generate ongoing program capacity independent of future grant cycles.

---

## SECTION V: INTENDED IMPACT AND MEASUREMENT

### Projected Outcomes

FAITH Foundation will measure program impact across five domains, with outcomes tracked longitudinally and reported quarterly:

**Housing Placement**
- Number of individuals and families transitioned from homelessness or unstable housing into transitional Cornerstone Communities units
- Number of program participants transitioned from transitional housing to permanent housing
- 30-, 60-, and 90-day housing retention rates for transitional program participants

**Financial Stability**
- Number of down payment assistance awards disbursed and total dollar value of awards
- Percentage of down payment assistance recipients maintaining stable housing at 12 months post-award

**Reentry Success**
- Number of formerly incarcerated individuals housed through Transitional Housing and Cornerstone Communities programs
- Employment placement rates among reentry participants within 90 days of program enrollment
- Recidivism comparison against regional baseline rates for reentry participants at 24 months

**Recovery Outcomes**
- Number of individuals in active recovery housed through the program
- Sobriety milestone maintenance rates among recovery housing participants
- Connection rates to ongoing treatment and peer support services

**Community Development**
- Number of Cornerstone Communities sites developed or expanded with grant funds
- Total modular housing units acquired and placed
- Occupancy rates and successful transitions from transitional to permanent housing per unit per year

[NEEDS INPUT: Year 1 numeric targets for participants served under this specific grant-funded program — e.g., number of households receiving down payment assistance, number of transitional housing units acquired, number of individuals housed — are required to complete this section. Targets should be proportionate to the requested grant amount and realistic given the organization's current stage of operations.]

### Data Collection and Reporting

All program data will be collected through FAITH Foundation's case management system and reported quarterly to the board of directors and, as required, to the funding agency. FAITH Foundation is committed to transparency in financial stewardship and program outcomes. The Foundation will maintain records of all grant expenditures, participant enrollment and outcomes, and housing asset deployment in compliance with CDBG reporting requirements.

---

## SECTION VI: ALIGNMENT WITH FUNDER PRIORITIES

This application directly addresses every priority identified in the Texas Community Development Block Grant – Housing funding opportunity:

| Funder Priority | FAITH Foundation Program Response |
|---|---|
| Affordable housing development | Cornerstone Communities Initiative: modular housing acquisition and site development in rural South Texas |
| Transitional housing programs | Transitional Housing Program: up to 24-month placements with case management for reentry, recovery, and veteran populations |
| Down payment assistance for low-income families | Down Payment Assistance Program: direct awards to employment-stable low-income individuals and families |
| Acquisition of modular housing units in rural Texas communities | Cornerstone Communities Initiative: purpose-built modular micro-communities on acquired or donated rural land |
| Reentry populations | Second Chance Reentry program component: dedicated transitional housing and case management for formerly incarcerated individuals |
| Individuals in recovery | Recovery Housing program component: structured transitional housing continuum for individuals in active recovery from addiction |
| Veterans experiencing housing insecurity | Veterans Path Home program component: dedicated housing assistance, VA benefits navigation, and case management for veterans |
| Rural Texas communities | Explicit geographic focus on rural South and Central Texas; modular deployment model specifically designed for rural development economics |

FAITH Foundation is not a general social services organization that has identified housing as an adjacent funding opportunity. It was built, from its founding, to address the precise intersection of rural affordable housing development, transitional housing for reentry and recovery populations, and veteran housing insecurity that this funding opportunity prioritizes. The founder's lived experience of incarceration, addiction, and recovery informs every program design decision the organization has made. The board's construction and housing industry expertise ensures that capital investments in modular housing acquisition and site development are managed with the accountability and competence that federal community development funding requires.
