knowledgeBase.title: Core mission statement
knowledgeBase.content: Hope Harbor Community Services helps Riverside Valley families move from housing instability to lasting self-sufficiency through emergency assistance, financial coaching, and affordable-housing navigation.

knowledgeBase.title: Housing instability in the Riverside Valley
knowledgeBase.content: 1 in 6 Riverside Valley families with children spends more than half its income on rent, leaving them one emergency away from eviction. Local shelters turn away families weekly for lack of capacity.

knowledgeBase.title: Housing stability outcomes
knowledgeBase.content: Of families completing our housing navigation program, 84% remained stably housed 12 months later and 71% increased their monthly income through coaching and benefits enrollment.

knowledgeBase.title: Organizational capacity & staffing
knowledgeBase.content: A 14-person staff including 6 credentialed case managers and 2 financial coaches, supported by 86 trained volunteers and an HMIS-integrated case-management system.

knowledgeBase.title: Diversified funding & sustainability
knowledgeBase.content: Revenue is diversified across government contracts (38%), foundations (29%), corporate giving (18%), and individual donors and events (15%), reducing reliance on any single source.

knowledgeBase.title: Mission Statement
knowledgeBase.content: The Foundation for Affordable Instruction and Tenancy Hope (FAITH Foundation) exists to help economically disadvantaged individuals and families achieve sustainable homeownership. We serve single mothers, veterans, individuals in recovery and re-entry, and other marginalized populations by providing down payment assistance vouchers, financial literacy education, and access to affordable modular housing. Our mission is to break the cycle of housing insecurity by combining direct financial assistance with comprehensive homebuyer education, empowering participants to build generational wealth through homeownership.

knowledgeBase.title: Vision Statement
knowledgeBase.content: The FAITH Foundation envisions a future where every economically disadvantaged family has a viable pathway to homeownership. We aim to become the leading national model for nonprofit-driven affordable housing by combining modular home technology, corporate giving partnerships, and wraparound financial education. Within five years we intend to help 500 families achieve homeownership across Texas and expand nationally.

knowledgeBase.title: Housing Affordability Crisis
knowledgeBase.content: The US faces a critical affordable housing shortage with over 7.3 million affordable rental homes missing nationwide. In Texas the median home price increased over 40 percent since 2020. Single mothers head 10 million households nationally with homeownership rates 30 points below married couples. Veterans face barriers including service-connected disabilities and employment gaps. Formerly incarcerated individuals encounter credit damage and landlord screening barriers. These populations are trapped in expensive rental cycles unable to save for down payments. Traditional assistance programs have long waitlists leaving a critical gap the FAITH Foundation addresses through voucher-based down payment assistance.

knowledgeBase.title: Down Payment Assistance Voucher Program
knowledgeBase.content: The FAITH Foundation provides vouchers of up to 2500 dollars toward down payment costs on discounted modular housing units through partner Bright Box Homes. Program pathway: (1) Application and eligibility screening (2) Enrollment in mandatory Financial Literacy and Credit Repair Education Seminars (3) Matching with modular home inventory at discounted rates (4) Voucher issuance and closing assistance. Available homes include 20x20 and 20x40 expandable container homes, Apple cabins and space capsule units.

knowledgeBase.title: Financial Literacy Education
knowledgeBase.content: The FAITH Foundation provides financial literacy and credit repair education seminars covering budgeting, credit reports, credit repair strategies, mortgage preparation, loan terms, homeownership financial planning, and avoiding predatory lending. Completion is prerequisite for voucher issuance. Offered in-person and virtual.

knowledgeBase.title: Land Acquisition and Site Development
knowledgeBase.content: Long-term goals include acquiring land for modular home communities, site development with utilities and infrastructure, sourcing materials through grants and donations, overseeing construction of modular homes, and creating planned affordable communities. Vertically integrated model controls costs passing savings to homebuyers.

knowledgeBase.title: Projected Community Impact
knowledgeBase.content: Each family saves 3000-5000 dollars annually transitioning to homeownership. Net worth increases 40x vs renting. Children score 9 percent higher in math and 7 percent higher in reading. Stable housing reduces ER visits by 18 percent. Every dollar in down payment assistance generates 16 dollars in local economic activity. Education seminars improve credit scores 50-80 points in 12 months. Veterans show 25 percent better VA treatment adherence. Re-entry participants show 43 percent lower recidivism.

knowledgeBase.title: Bright Box Homes Strategic Partnership
knowledgeBase.content: Bright Box Homes donates 2500 dollars to FAITH Foundation for every home sold through any channel. Offers modular housing at discounted rates to voucher recipients. Models include 20x20 and 20x40 expandable container homes, Apple cabins and space capsule units. Partnership aligns both missions.

knowledgeBase.title: Have you received previous funding?
knowledgeBase.content: Faith Foundation is in its inaugural funding cycle. The organization was established to address critical gaps in rural South Texas housing infrastructure, with initial operations funded through founder investment and church community support.

knowledgeBase.title: Organizational Capacity
knowledgeBase.content: FAITH Foundation is a certified 501c3 statutory foundation incorporated in Wyoming, EIN 33-2640449, at 209 Surecast Drive Suite 105 Burnet Texas 78611. Phone 888-497-6620. Founded 18 months ago with Supabase data management, Benavora grant platform, and corporate partnerships. Lean overhead with leadership in real estate, construction, and community development.

knowledgeBase.title: Financial Sustainability Model
knowledgeBase.content: Cornerstone is Bright Box Homes partnership donating 2500 dollars per home sold. Supplemented by grants, donations, government programs (HOME, CDBG), and CDFI partnerships. Self-reinforcing model where home purchases generate Foundation funding. Land acquisition builds appreciating assets reducing per-unit costs.

knowledgeBase.title: Founding and Development
knowledgeBase.content: FAITH Foundation established 18 months ago as 501c3 in Wyoming. Founding vision combined direct voucher assistance, financial education, and affordable modular housing access. Since founding: secured certification, established Bright Box partnership, developed voucher program, launched financial literacy curriculum, deployed Benavora platform, begun outreach across central Texas.

knowledgeBase.title: Program Budget Framework
knowledgeBase.content: Four areas: Direct Assistance (vouchers at 2500 per family), Education Programs (instructors, materials, venues, virtual platforms), Housing Development (land, site prep, modular homes, construction), Operations (staff, technology, insurance, legal, admin below 15 percent). Voucher funding flows entirely to participants. Housing development generates appreciating assets.

knowledgeBase.title: what is your organization's mission statement?
knowledgeBase.content: The FAITH Foundation exists to break the cycle of housing insecurity by providing financial education, homeownership instruction, and direct housing assistance to veterans, individuals experiencing homelessness, single parents, those in recovery, those reentering society, and other economically disadvantaged populations. Through our strategic partnership with Bright Box Homes, we transform charitable giving into permanent, affordable housing solutions

knowledgeBase.title: How do you measure impact?
knowledgeBase.content: Impact is measured across five domains: (1) Housing Placement — number of individuals and families transitioned from homelessness or unstable housing into transitional units and permanent housing, tracked by 30/60/90-day retention rates. (2) Financial Stability — number of down payment assistance awards disbursed, average award amount, and percentage of recipients maintaining housing at 12 months. (3) Reentry Success — number of formerly incarcerated individuals housed, employment placement rates, and recidivism reduction compared to regional averages. (4) Recovery Outcomes — number of individuals in active recovery housed through the program, sobriety milestones maintained, and connection rates to ongoing treatment and support services. (5) Community Development — number of Cornerstone Communities sites developed, total modular housing units acquired and placed, occupancy rates, and successful transitions from transitional to permanent housing. All outcomes tracked longitudinally with quarterly reporting and annual program evaluation.

knowledgeBase.title: What makes your organization unique?
knowledgeBase.content: The Cornerstone Communities model — purpose-built transitional micro-communities that provide structured pathways from emergency shelter to permanent housing

knowledgeBase.title: How will funds be used?
knowledgeBase.content: Down payment assistance for qualifying individuals and families, transitional housing placement, case management and supportive services, acquisition of modular and manufactured housing units for Cornerstone Communities, site development and infrastructure for micro-community housing, and operational support for housing navigation and reentry programming.

knowledgeBase.title: What is your geographic service area?
knowledgeBase.content: South & Central Texas and the Texas Gulf Coast region, with primary focus on rural and underserved communities

knowledgeBase.title: what population do you serve?
knowledgeBase.content: Economically disadvantaged individuals, those reentering society from incarceration, people in addiction recovery, and families facing housing insecurity in Texas

knowledgeBase.title: What partnerships do you have?
knowledgeBase.content: Faith Foundation partners with local churches, recovery programs, reentry service providers, county social services agencies, and housing authorities across South Texas. We collaborate with building material suppliers, modular housing manufacturers, and land owners to reduce development costs for Cornerstone Communities.

knowledgeBase.title: What are your organization's greatest needs
knowledgeBase.content: Land acquisition or donation for Cornerstone Communities development sites, building materials and modular housing unit donations, construction labor volunteers, down payment assistance funding, operational funding for case management staff, and in-kind donations of furnishings and household essentials for transitional housing units.

knowledgeBase.title: Do you accept in-kind donations?
knowledgeBase.content: Yes. Faith Foundation actively seeks donations of land, building materials, modular and manufactured housing units, construction equipment and labor, furnishings, appliances, household goods, and professional services including legal, architectural, surveying, and construction management.

knowledgeBase.title: What is your sustainability plan?
knowledgeBase.content: Cornerstone Communities generate long-term sustainability through a rotating housing model — as residents transition to permanent housing, units become available for new participants. Revenue streams include program fees on a sliding scale, rental income from stabilized units, recurring grant funding, corporate sponsorships, church partnerships, and individual donor cultivation. Physical assets — land and housing units — appreciate and reduce ongoing capital needs."

knowledgeBase.title: Who is on your leadership team
knowledgeBase.content:
Pastor Juan Valdez serves as Secretary and Protector of the Faith Foundation, providing spiritual oversight, governance accountability, and mission stewardship for the organization. With more than 40 years of Christian faith and nearly 30 years of ordained ministry experience, Pastor Valdez offers a lifetime of leadership grounded in biblical principles, service, and integrity.
His ministry has extended across the United States, South America, Central America, the Caribbean, and Africa, where he has taught, preached, and supported faith-based outreach initiatives. Known for his wisdom, humility, and commitment to discipleship, Pastor Valdez has dedicated his life to helping individuals and families discover hope, purpose, and restoration through faith.
Beyond ministry, Pastor Valdez and his wife, Martha, demonstrated an extraordinary commitment to their community through business ownership, operating a successful hair studio in the same San Antonio location for 34 years. Such longevity reflects the consistency, reliability, and stewardship that have characterized both his professional and ministry endeavors throughout his life.
As a member of the Foundation's leadership team, Pastor Valdez helps safeguard the organization's mission, values, and charitable purpose while providing counsel on matters of governance, ethics, and spiritual direction. His experience, character, and servant-hearted leadership make him a trusted voice in advancing the Foundation's commitment to affordable housing, education, and community empowerment.
Pastor Valdez currently serves as an Associate Pastor at Temple of Praise and resides in Texas with his wife, Martha. Together they have built a legacy of faith that spans generations, including three daughters, six grandchildren, and two great-grandchildren. His lifelong dedication to faith, family, ministry, and community service continues to exemplify the values upon which the Faith Foundation was established.

Scott Ellis serves as Treasurer and Board Chair of the Faith Foundation, providing financial oversight, strategic guidance, and leadership in support of the Foundation's mission to expand affordable housing opportunities and strengthen communities through faith-based service.
Scott is the owner of E4 Roofing & Construction, a Georgetown, Texas-based company he has successfully led for more than 15 years. Through his business leadership, he has earned a reputation for integrity, accountability, and a commitment to serving customers with excellence. His experience as a business owner provides the Foundation with valuable financial, operational, project management, and organizational expertise.
In addition to his business leadership, Scott brings practical construction and housing industry knowledge that directly supports the Foundation's mission. His experience in residential and commercial construction, project coordination, budgeting, contractor management, and building systems provides valuable insight as the Foundation develops affordable housing initiatives and evaluates housing-related opportunities. His understanding of construction costs, building practices, property improvement, and long-term asset stewardship helps ensure that projects are approached responsibly, efficiently, and with a focus on maximizing community impact.
A longtime resident of Georgetown, Texas, Scott has called the community home for more than 24 years. He and his wife, Christy, have been married for 37 years and have raised two daughters together. Their enduring commitment to faith, family, and community reflects the values that guide both their personal and professional lives.
Scott and Christy are active members of their local church, where they have dedicated themselves to serving others through ministry, fellowship, and community engagement. Scott is actively involved in Bible studies and men's groups, encouraging spiritual growth, mentorship, accountability, and Christian leadership. He has also participated in mission work in Mexico, demonstrating a servant's heart and a commitment to helping others beyond his local community.
As Treasurer and Board Chair, Scott helps ensure that the Faith Foundation remains a faithful steward of its resources while advancing its vision of increasing access to affordable housing and creating opportunities for individuals and families to achieve long-term stability. His combination of business leadership, construction expertise, financial stewardship, and Christian service makes him a trusted leader and an invaluable member of the Foundation's governing team.



Reid Whitesides is the Founder, President, and Executive Director of The Faith Foundation, an organization dedicated to helping individuals experiencing homelessness, recovery, and reentry build stable, self-sufficient futures through affordable housing and supportive opportunities.
With more than 20 years of experience in construction, roofing, project management, sales, consulting, and housing-related industries, Reid brings practical expertise to the Foundation's mission of creating sustainable pathways to stability and independence. He also has a passion for technology and spends much of his spare time developing websites, software applications, and automation tools that support nonprofit, housing, and community-focused initiatives.
His commitment to this work is deeply personal. During a long struggle with addiction, Reid spent nearly twenty years incarcerated in the State of Texas. Those experiences gave him firsthand insight into the challenges many face when rebuilding their lives after addiction, incarceration, and homelessness. Today, he has been sober for more than fifteen years and is dedicated to helping others overcome similar barriers.
Reid credits his Christian faith and God's transformative work in his life as the foundation of his recovery and purpose. He believes stable housing is often the first step toward lasting change and that every person deserves the opportunity to build a better future, regardless of their past.
Today, he leads The Faith Foundation with a simple conviction: that lives can be transformed when people are given access to hope, opportunity, and a stable foundation on which to build their future.

knowledgeBase.title: Impact Statement
knowledgeBase.content:
Organizational Stage
FAITH Foundation is a newly established 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization in its founding year of operations. As a pre-revenue organization, we have not yet produced measurable program outcomes. This impact statement therefore defines the outcomes we intend to achieve, the metrics by which we will measure success, and the targets we have set for our first three years of operation. All projected outcomes are based on evidence-based models documented by HUD, the VA, and peer organizations operating similar housing voucher and community development programs.
Intended Outcomes
Year 1 Targets (Founding Year)
•	Distribute 10 down payment assistance vouchers ($2,500 each) to qualifying families, totaling $25,000 in direct housing assistance.
•	Enroll 25 families in homeownership counseling and financial literacy programming.
•	Provide emergency bridge housing assistance to 15 families facing immediate housing crises.
•	Establish partnerships with a minimum of 3 local employers for reentry and recovery program participants.
•	Secure the first donated land parcel for Cornerstone Communities development.
•	Complete the Benavora-powered grant application system and submit a minimum of 10 competitive grant applications.
•	Achieve Google Ad Grants approval and deploy targeted campaigns for housing voucher awareness.
•	Recruit and train 20 volunteers for mentorship, financial literacy instruction, and community outreach.
Year 2 Targets
•	Distribute 40 housing vouchers, totaling $100,000 in direct assistance.
•	Graduate 20 families from homeownership counseling into active homebuyers.
•	Begin construction on the first Cornerstone Community with on-site programming.
•	Expand recovery housing partnerships to serve 30 individuals annually.
•	Place 15 reentry participants into stable employment within 90 days of program enrollment.
•	Achieve a 90% housing retention rate among voucher recipients at the 12-month mark.
Year 3 Targets
•	Distribute 100 housing vouchers, totaling $250,000 in direct assistance.
•	Complete and occupy the first Cornerstone Community with a minimum of 20 residential units.
•	Achieve a homeownership conversion rate of 30% among program participants who entered in Year 1.
•	Expand geographic service area beyond initial Texas communities.
•	Establish a second Bright Box Homes-style corporate partnership generating recurring voucher funding.
•	Publish the first annual impact report with independently verified outcome data.
How We Measure Success
FAITH Foundation will track and report on the following key performance indicators (KPIs) across all programs:
•	Vouchers Distributed: Total number and dollar value of down payment and housing vouchers issued per quarter.
•	Housing Retention Rate: Percentage of voucher recipients who remain stably housed at 6-month and 12-month intervals after receiving assistance.
•	Homeownership Conversion Rate: Percentage of program participants who transition from rental housing to homeownership within 24 months of enrollment.
•	Financial Readiness Score: Measured improvement in credit score, debt-to-income ratio, and savings rate among financial literacy program completers.
•	Employment Placement Rate: Percentage of reentry and recovery participants placed in employment within 90 days of program enrollment.
•	Recidivism Prevention Rate: Percentage of reentry participants who avoid reincarceration within 24 months of program completion.
•	Recovery Stability Rate: Percentage of recovery housing participants who maintain sobriety and stable housing at 12-month intervals.
•	Volunteer Hours and Mentorship Matches: Total volunteer engagement hours and number of active mentor-mentee relationships.
•	Grant Success Rate: Percentage of grant applications funded and total grant revenue generated through Benavora.
•	Cornerstone Communities Occupancy: Number of units built, occupied, and percentage of residents progressing toward homeownership.
Data Collection and Reporting
All program data will be collected through FAITH Foundation’s case management system and reported quarterly to the board of directors. Annual impact reports will be published on our website and made available to all funders, donors, and stakeholders. FAITH Foundation is committed to transparency in both financial stewardship and program outcomes, and we will pursue third-party outcome verification beginning in Year 2.
Long-Term Vision
Within five years, FAITH Foundation intends to be the leading housing voucher and community development organization serving veterans, reentry, recovery, and single-parent populations in Texas. Our Cornerstone Communities model is designed to be replicable in any state where donated land and housing inventory shortages intersect. By demonstrating measurable outcomes in homeownership conversion, housing retention, and community stability, we intend to establish the evidence base for scaling this model through federal, state, and private funding partnerships. The ultimate measure of our success is not how many families we serve temporarily, but how many families we move permanently into homes they own.

knowledgeBase.title: What is your theory of change?
knowledgeBase.content: Stable housing is the foundation for all other recovery, and we believe that foundation begins with God's grace. Faith Foundation operates on the biblical principle that every person — regardless of past mistakes, addiction, incarceration, or poverty — deserves dignity, shelter, and a second chance through Christ's redemptive love. By providing immediate transitional shelter through Cornerstone Communities, paired with faith-based case management, spiritual mentorship, financial literacy, and down payment assistance, individuals rebuild their lives on solid ground — physically and spiritually. Each successful transition is a testimony to God's provision and creates capacity for the next person He brings through our doors.

knowledgeBase.title: How do you serve rural communities specifically?
knowledgeBase.content: Rural South Texas faces acute housing shortages with limited nonprofit infrastructure. Faith Foundation addresses this through modular housing deployment — units can be sited on donated or acquired rural land without the delays and costs of traditional construction. This approach brings housing solutions directly to underserved rural communities rather than concentrating resources in urban centers.

knowledgeBase.title: What are your capital needs?
knowledgeBase.content: Land parcels suitable for micro-community development, modular housing units ($30,000-$60,000 per unit), site preparation and utility infrastructure, community common spaces, and program vehicles for rural case management outreach.

knowledgeBase.title: What is your theory of change? (secular version)
knowledgeBase.content: Stable housing is the prerequisite for sustained recovery from addiction, successful community reentry after incarceration, and long-term economic self-sufficiency. Faith Foundation's model addresses the root cause of cyclical homelessness — the absence of affordable transitional housing in rural communities. By deploying modular housing units in purpose-built Cornerstone Communities, paired with case management, peer mentorship, financial literacy, and down payment assistance, individuals progress through a structured pathway from crisis to stability to permanent housing. Each successful transition frees capacity for the next participant, creating a self-sustaining cycle of community impact.

Faith Foundation envisions a network of Cornerstone Communities across South Texas and beyond, each serving as a model for how modular housing, faith-based mentorship, and wraparound support services can permanently break the cycle of homelessness for the most vulnerable populations.

Indirect costs are maintained below 15 percent of total program budget and cover organizational administration, accounting, reporting, and compliance. In-kind donations of building materials, volunteer labor, and professional services significantly reduce cash outlays and are documented at fair market value for matching fund requirements.

knowledgeBase.title: Need Statement
knowledgeBase.content:
The National Housing Crisis by the Numbers
The United States is experiencing a housing crisis of historic proportions. The evidence is not anecdotal; it is documented across every federal data source and research institution tracking housing stability in America.
Homelessness
•	745,652 people were experiencing homelessness on a single night in January 2025, including 266,320 living unsheltered. (HUD 2025 Annual Homelessness Assessment Report)
•	Homelessness increased 18% between 2023 and 2024 before declining 3.3% in 2025, representing the first overall decrease since 2016. (National Alliance to End Homelessness, 2025)
•	Chronic homelessness increased 2.1% in 2025, and homelessness among adults aged 65 and older increased 6.8%. (HUD 2025 AHAR)
•	African Americans make up 14.4% of the U.S. population but represent 32.7% of the homeless population. (HUD 2025 AHAR)
•	The homelessness response system has permanent housing units for only 9.5% of people in need, and only enough capacity to house 16% of households currently in shelter. (National Alliance to End Homelessness, 2025)
•	64% of all people experiencing homelessness live in just 7 states: California, Illinois, Texas, Massachusetts, Florida, Washington, and New York. (HUD 2024 AHAR)
Texas-Specific Data
•	Nearly 28,000 Texans were experiencing homelessness in the 2024 Point-in-Time count, including 1,837 veterans. (HUD 2024 AHAR, cited in Texas HB 158)
•	44% of Texans experiencing homelessness were unsheltered, meaning they had no access to emergency shelter or transitional housing. (HUD 2024 AHAR)
•	4,085 veterans were served by Texas Continuums of Care as of December 2023, up from 3,962 in 2022. (Texas Homeless Data Sharing Network)
•	2,594 individuals were identified as chronically homeless in Texas in 2023, up from 1,949 in 2022. (Texas Homeless Data Sharing Network)
Veteran Housing Instability
•	32,882 veterans were experiencing homelessness on a single night in January 2024, a record low since measurement began in 2009 but still representing tens of thousands of individuals who served their country. (VA 2024 PIT Count)
•	13,851 veterans were unsheltered in 2024. (VA 2024 PIT Count)
•	Black veterans make up 14% of the overall veteran population but represent 31% of homeless veterans. (Mission Roll Call, 2024)
•	California, Florida, and Texas have the highest concentrations of homeless veterans, with California alone accounting for 30% of all homeless veterans nationally. (Mission Roll Call, 2024)
•	In Texas, veteran homelessness decreased 9.7% between 2023 and 2024, from 2,036 to 1,837. (VA/HUD 2024 PIT Count)
Reentry and Formerly Incarcerated Populations
•	Formerly incarcerated people are approximately 10 times more likely to experience homelessness than the general population. (National Low Income Housing Coalition, 2018; Prison Policy Initiative)
•	Formerly incarcerated individuals make up between 23.1% and 47.8% of annual homeless shelter admissions. (Community Solutions / CSG Justice Center, 2019)
•	In North Carolina, 28% of people released from state prisons in 2024 were released directly into homelessness. (NC Reentry Housing Assessment, 2025)
•	82% of individuals released from prison across 24 states were re-arrested within 10 years of release. (UNLV Reentry Research Brief, 2024)
•	Nearly 450,000 individuals were released from state and federal prisons in 2021 alone, and on average, a formerly incarcerated individual spends over 6 months unemployed post-release. (UNLV Reentry Research Brief)
•	People experiencing homelessness after release are at increased risk of reincarceration due to more frequent law enforcement contact and supervision violations related to their housing status. (CSG Justice Center, 2025)
•	The nation faces a shortage of 7.3 million rental units affordable and available to extremely low-income households, compounding the barriers for people with criminal records who are already excluded from most private housing. (National Low Income Housing Coalition)
Single-Parent Homeownership Gap
•	The homeownership rate among single mothers is approximately 34%, compared to 49% for single fathers and 84% for married couples without children. (U.S. Census Bureau ACS / LendingTree, 2024)
•	Single-parent households face estimated home prices approaching five times their income, indicating severe housing cost burden. (NAHB Eye on Housing, 2024)
•	Single women made up 19% of all homebuyers in 2023 and own 20.3 million homes nationwide, but single mothers with dependent children face significantly lower ownership rates due to childcare costs and single-income limitations. (National Association of Realtors, 2023; U.S. Census Bureau)
The Down Payment Barrier
•	First-time homebuyers now make up just 21% of the market, the lowest share since NAR began tracking in 1981. Before 2008, they consistently accounted for about 40%. (NAR 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers)
•	The median age of first-time homebuyers has climbed to a record 40 years old, up from the late 20s in the 1980s. (NAR 2025 Profile)
•	67% of millennials have no savings for a home down payment. (REsimpli 2025 Market Survey)
•	75% of first-time homebuyers cited affordability as their top concern, and more than 40% said student loans make it harder to save for a down payment. (REsimpli 2025 Market Survey)
•	The median down payment for first-time buyers is 9%, compared to 23% for repeat purchasers, reflecting wealth inequality across generations. (NAR 2025 Profile)
•	74.2% of homeowner households with incomes below $30,000 are cost-burdened, paying more than 30% of income on housing, the highest rate in over 20 years. (Joint Center for Housing Studies, Harvard University, 2023 data)
•	The Black homeownership rate (46.6%) and Hispanic homeownership rate (49.9%) remain significantly below the white homeownership rate (74.0%) as of Q1 2024. (Joint Center for Housing Studies, Harvard University)
The Gap FAITH Foundation Fills
The data reveals two interconnected failures. First, there is insufficient housing inventory affordable to the populations we serve. Second, there is insufficient financial assistance to bridge the gap between rental instability and homeownership. Most existing programs address one or the other. FAITH Foundation addresses both: the demand side through direct down payment vouchers and housing counseling, and the supply side through our Cornerstone Communities land acquisition and development initiative. No other organization in our service area provides this integrated, both-sides approach with a self-sustaining funding mechanism tied to new home construction.

knowledgeBase.title: Core Programs Overview
knowledgeBase.content: Faith Foundation operates three interconnected housing programs across South Texas. The Down Payment Assistance Program provides direct financial awards to qualifying low-income individuals and families to secure permanent housing, targeting those who are employment-stable but lack savings for upfront housing costs. The Transitional Housing Program places individuals exiting homelessness, incarceration, or addiction treatment into stable transitional units with case management support, financial literacy training, and peer mentorship for up to 24 months. The Cornerstone Communities Initiative is the Foundation's flagship development program, acquiring land and deploying modular and manufactured housing units to create purpose-built micro-communities designed specifically for transitional residents. Each Cornerstone Community includes individual housing units, shared community spaces, and on-site access to case management and support services. As residents stabilize and transition to permanent housing, their units become available for new participants, creating a self-sustaining cycle of community impact. All programs prioritize military veterans, formerly incarcerated individuals reentering society, people in addiction recovery, single-parent families, and individuals experiencing or at risk of homelessness in rural and underserved South Texas communities.

knowledgeBase.title: Sustainability Plan
knowledgeBase.content: Faith Foundation's long-term sustainability is built on a rotating housing asset model. Cornerstone Communities generate ongoing capacity as residents transition to permanent housing and units become available for new participants. Revenue streams include program fees assessed on a sliding scale based on participant income, rental income from stabilized housing units, recurring grant funding from federal, state, and private sources, corporate sponsorships and in-kind donations, church partnerships and congregational giving, and individual donor cultivation. Physical assets including land and modular housing units appreciate over time and reduce ongoing capital expenditure requirements. The Foundation actively pursues diversified funding across government grants, private foundations, corporate giving programs, faith-based funders, and community development financial institutions to avoid dependency on any single source. Operational costs are controlled through volunteer labor, donated materials, and shared administrative infrastructure across program sites.

knowledgeBase.title: Mission Statement
knowledgeBase.content:
Core Mission
FAITH Foundation (Foundation for Affordable Instruction and Tenancy Hope) exists to dismantle the barriers between housing instability and permanent homeownership for populations systemically excluded from the American dream of owning a home. We serve military veterans, individuals in addiction recovery, formerly incarcerated citizens reentering society, single-parent families, and individuals experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Our mission is not to provide temporary shelter but to build a complete, permanent pathway from crisis to homeownership through direct down payment assistance vouchers, housing counseling, financial literacy education, and the development of purpose-built residential communities on donated land.
Why We Exist
The affordable housing crisis in the United States is not a single problem. It is a compounding failure across multiple systems: a national shortage of 7.3 million rental units affordable to extremely low-income households, a homeownership market where the median age of first-time buyers has risen to a record 40 years old, and a down payment gap that locks out the families who would benefit most from the wealth-building stability of owning a home. For the populations FAITH Foundation serves, these barriers are multiplied by service-connected disabilities, criminal records, addiction histories, single-income households, and the cascading effects of housing instability on employment, health, and family cohesion.
Traditional nonprofit housing models address only one side of this equation. They provide rental assistance, emergency shelter, or counseling, but stop short of homeownership. FAITH Foundation operates on a fundamentally different thesis: that the people we serve do not merely need a place to stay; they need a home they own. Homeownership is the single most effective vehicle for long-term stability, intergenerational wealth building, and community investment. Our model is designed to move families not just out of crisis, but into ownership.
Our Model
FAITH Foundation operates an integrated ecosystem of eight interconnected programs, all orbiting a single objective: homeownership. Each program addresses a different stage of the journey from instability to ownership, and families may enter through any door. The model is sustained in part by a renewable funding mechanism: our partnership with Bright Box Homes, a container home builder that donates $2,500 to FAITH Foundation for every home sold. These donations fund the housing vouchers that help the next family into a home, creating a self-reinforcing cycle of community investment.
Program Ecosystem
•	Homeownership Counseling: Our flagship program providing pre-purchase counseling, mortgage readiness, and buyer education to prepare families for sustainable homeownership.
•	Down Payment and Housing Vouchers: Direct financial assistance funded by Bright Box Homes donations, providing $2,500 vouchers toward down payments and rental deposits for qualifying families.
•	Emergency Bridge Housing: Rapid rental and deposit assistance for families facing sudden housing crises, preventing evictions before they cascade into homelessness.
•	Veterans Path Home: Rental assistance, VA benefits navigation, and dedicated case management for military veterans transitioning from housing instability to permanent homes.
•	Recovery Housing: A structured continuum from sober living through transitional housing to permanent independent housing, with on-site support groups and accountability at every stage.
•	Second Chance Reentry: Transitional housing, employment support, and case management for formerly incarcerated individuals rebuilding stability after release.
•	Single Parent Stability: Affordable housing assistance paired with childcare navigation and financial coaching for single-parent families working toward homeownership.
•	Financial Literacy: Hands-on budgeting, credit-building, and debt management education that prepares families to qualify for and sustain homeownership.
Cornerstone Communities Initiative
Beyond direct voucher assistance, FAITH Foundation addresses the supply side of the housing crisis through our Cornerstone Communities initiative. We acquire donated land from private owners, churches, municipalities, and developers, then develop purpose-built residential communities through competitive open-bid construction. Each Cornerstone Community includes on-site wraparound services such as recovery programming, remote work and learning centers, community laundry facilities, shuttle transportation, and dedicated case management. Residents enter as transitional housing participants and graduate into permanent homeownership through FAITH’s voucher pipeline. This initiative creates the affordable housing inventory that vouchers alone cannot produce.
Faith-Based Foundation
FAITH Foundation is rooted in the belief that every person deserves the dignity of a stable home. Our work is guided by the principle that faith without works is incomplete, and that the most meaningful expression of faith is meeting people where they are with tangible, measurable support that changes the trajectory of their lives and the lives of their children. We serve all people regardless of religious affiliation, and our programs are designed to be inclusive, evidence-informed, and outcome-driven.
Geographic Focus
FAITH Foundation currently serves families across the state of Texas, with a focus on communities where affordable housing inventory is critically low and where the populations we serve are concentrated. Texas is home to nearly 28,000 people experiencing homelessness, including 1,837 veterans, with 44% of the state’s homeless population living unsheltered. Our long-term vision is to expand the Cornerstone Communities model to other states where land donation partnerships and housing inventory shortages create opportunities for replication.

knowledgeBase.title: Founding and History
knowledgeBase.content: Faith Foundation was established by Reid Whitesides to address the critical shortage of affordable and transitional housing options in rural South Texas communities. The organization was founded on the conviction that stable housing is the essential foundation for recovery from addiction, successful reentry after incarceration, and long-term economic self-sufficiency. The Foundation's name reflects its founding purpose: the Foundation for Affordable Instruction and Tenancy Hope. Drawing on the founder's background in real estate and construction, the organization developed the Cornerstone Communities model as an innovative approach to deploying affordable housing at scale in rural areas where traditional development is cost-prohibitive. The model uses modular and manufactured housing units sited on acquired or donated land to create purpose-built transitional micro-communities. Faith Foundation operates as a 508(c)(1)(a) faith-based organization, grounding its mission in Christian principles of grace, redemption, and service while maintaining open enrollment for all individuals regardless of faith background

knowledgeBase.title: Impact Statement
knowledgeBase.content:
Organizational Stage
FAITH Foundation is a newly established 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization in its founding year of operations. As a pre-revenue organization, we have not yet produced measurable program outcomes. This impact statement therefore defines the outcomes we intend to achieve, the metrics by which we will measure success, and the targets we have set for our first three years of operation. All projected outcomes are based on evidence-based models documented by HUD, the VA, and peer organizations operating similar housing voucher and community development programs.
Intended Outcomes
Year 1 Targets (Founding Year)
•	Distribute 10 down payment assistance vouchers ($2,500 each) to qualifying families, totaling $25,000 in direct housing assistance.
•	Enroll 25 families in homeownership counseling and financial literacy programming.
•	Provide emergency bridge housing assistance to 15 families facing immediate housing crises.
•	Establish partnerships with a minimum of 3 local employers for reentry and recovery program participants.
•	Secure the first donated land parcel for Cornerstone Communities development.
•	Complete the Benavora-powered grant application system and submit a minimum of 10 competitive grant applications.
•	Achieve Google Ad Grants approval and deploy targeted campaigns for housing voucher awareness.
•	Recruit and train 20 volunteers for mentorship, financial literacy instruction, and community outreach.
Year 2 Targets
•	Distribute 40 housing vouchers, totaling $100,000 in direct assistance.
•	Graduate 20 families from homeownership counseling into active homebuyers.
•	Begin construction on the first Cornerstone Community with on-site programming.
•	Expand recovery housing partnerships to serve 30 individuals annually.
•	Place 15 reentry participants into stable employment within 90 days of program enrollment.
•	Achieve a 90% housing retention rate among voucher recipients at the 12-month mark.
Year 3 Targets
•	Distribute 100 housing vouchers, totaling $250,000 in direct assistance.
•	Complete and occupy the first Cornerstone Community with a minimum of 20 residential units.
•	Achieve a homeownership conversion rate of 30% among program participants who entered in Year 1.
•	Expand geographic service area beyond initial Texas communities.
•	Establish a second Bright Box Homes-style corporate partnership generating recurring voucher funding.
•	Publish the first annual impact report with independently verified outcome data.
How We Measure Success
FAITH Foundation will track and report on the following key performance indicators (KPIs) across all programs:
•	Vouchers Distributed: Total number and dollar value of down payment and housing vouchers issued per quarter.
•	Housing Retention Rate: Percentage of voucher recipients who remain stably housed at 6-month and 12-month intervals after receiving assistance.
•	Homeownership Conversion Rate: Percentage of program participants who transition from rental housing to homeownership within 24 months of enrollment.
•	Financial Readiness Score: Measured improvement in credit score, debt-to-income ratio, and savings rate among financial literacy program completers.
•	Employment Placement Rate: Percentage of reentry and recovery participants placed in employment within 90 days of program enrollment.
•	Recidivism Prevention Rate: Percentage of reentry participants who avoid reincarceration within 24 months of program completion.
•	Recovery Stability Rate: Percentage of recovery housing participants who maintain sobriety and stable housing at 12-month intervals.
•	Volunteer Hours and Mentorship Matches: Total volunteer engagement hours and number of active mentor-mentee relationships.
•	Grant Success Rate: Percentage of grant applications funded and total grant revenue generated through Benavora.
•	Cornerstone Communities Occupancy: Number of units built, occupied, and percentage of residents progressing toward homeownership.
Data Collection and Reporting
All program data will be collected through FAITH Foundation’s case management system and reported quarterly to the board of directors. Annual impact reports will be published on our website and made available to all funders, donors, and stakeholders. FAITH Foundation is committed to transparency in both financial stewardship and program outcomes, and we will pursue third-party outcome verification beginning in Year 2.
Long-Term Vision
Within five years, FAITH Foundation intends to be the leading housing voucher and community development organization serving veterans, reentry, recovery, and single-parent populations in Texas. Our Cornerstone Communities model is designed to be replicable in any state where donated land and housing inventory shortages intersect. By demonstrating measurable outcomes in homeownership conversion, housing retention, and community stability, we intend to establish the evidence base for scaling this model through federal, state, and private funding partnerships. The ultimate measure of our success is not how many families we serve temporarily, but how many families we move permanently into homes they own.

Recovery program partners refer individuals completing treatment who need stable transitional housing, and provide ongoing support services for residents in active recovery. Reentry service partners coordinate with the Foundation to place formerly incarcerated individuals into transitional housing upon release, connecting them with employment services, legal aid, and family reunification support. County social services agencies and local housing authorities refer eligible families and individuals, coordinate benefits enrollment, and provide case management collaboration. Building material suppliers and modular housing manufacturers provide discounted or donated materials and units for Cornerstone Communities development. Land owners in rural South Texas communities donate or sell land at reduced cost for community development sites. Veterans service organizations refer military veterans experiencing housing insecurity and coordinate VA benefits enrollment.

knowledgeBase.title: Founding and History
knowledgeBase.content: Faith Foundation was established by Reid Whitesides to address the critical shortage of affordable and transitional housing options in rural South Texas communities. The organization was founded on the conviction that stable housing is the essential foundation for recovery from addiction, successful reentry after incarceration, and long-term economic self-sufficiency. The Foundation's name reflects its founding purpose: the Foundation for Affordable Instruction and Tenancy Hope. Drawing on the founder's background in real estate and construction, the organization developed the Cornerstone Communities model as an innovative approach to deploying affordable housing at scale in rural areas where traditional development is cost-prohibitive. The model uses modular and manufactured housing units sited on acquired or donated land to create purpose-built transitional micro-communities. Faith Foundation operates as a 508(c)(1)(a) faith-based organization, grounding its mission in Christian principles of grace, redemption, and service while maintaining open enrollment for all individuals regardless of faith background

knowledgeBase.title: Strategic Partner: Bright Box Homes
knowledgeBase.content: Through its strategic partnership with Bright Box Homes, FAITH Foundation transforms charitable giving into permanent, affordable housing solutions. Bright Box Homes supplies the modular and manufactured housing units deployed in the Foundation's Cornerstone Communities, enabling charitable contributions to be converted directly into durable, move-in-ready homes for the families the Foundation serves.

knowledgeBase.title: Board Leadership & Governance
knowledgeBase.content:
Reid Whitesides, Founder & President: Reid Whitesides is the Founder and President The Faith Foundation, an organization dedicated to helping individuals experiencing homelessness, recovery, and reentry build stable, self-sufficient futures through affordable housing and supportive opportunities.  With more than 20 years of experience in construction, roofing, project management, sales, consulting, and housing-related industries, Reid brings practical expertise to the Foundation's mission of creating sustainable pathways to stability and independence.  His commitment to this work is deeply personal. During a long struggle with addiction, Reid spent nearly twenty years incarcerated in the State of Texas. Those experiences gave him firsthand insight into the challenges many face when rebuilding their lives after addiction, incarceration, and homelessness. Today, he has been sober for more than fifteen years and is dedicated to helping others overcome similar barriers.  Reid credits his Christian faith and God's transformative work in his life as the foundation of his recovery and purpose. He believes stable housing is often the first step toward lasting change and that every person deserves the opportunity to build a better future, regardless of their past.

Pastor Juan Valdez, Secretary & Protector: Pastor Juan Valdez serves as Secretary and Protector of the Faith Foundation, providing spiritual oversight, governance accountability, and mission stewardship for the organization. With more than 40 years of Christian faith and nearly 30 years of ordained ministry experience, Pastor Valdez offers a lifetime of leadership grounded in biblical principles, service, and integrity. His ministry has extended across the United States, South America, Central America, the Caribbean, and Africa, where he has taught, preached, and supported faith-based outreach initiatives. Known for his wisdom, humility, and commitment to discipleship, Pastor Valdez has dedicated his life to helping individuals and families discover hope, purpose, and restoration through faith. Beyond ministry, Pastor Valdez and his wife, Martha, demonstrated an extraordinary commitment to their community through business ownership, operating a successful hair studio in the same San Antonio location for 34 years. Such longevity reflects the consistency, reliability, and stewardship that have characterized both his professional and ministry endeavors throughout his life. As a member of the Foundation's leadership team, Pastor Valdez helps safeguard the organization's mission, values, and charitable purpose while providing counsel on matters of governance, ethics, and spiritual direction. His experience, character, and servant-hearted leadership make him a trusted voice in advancing the Foundation's commitment to affordable housing, education, and community empowerment. Pastor Valdez currently serves as an Associate Pastor at Temple of Praise and resides in Texas with his wife, Martha. Together they have built a legacy of faith that spans generations, including three daughters, six grandchildren, and two great-grandchildren. His lifelong dedication to faith, family, ministry, and community service continues to exemplify the values upon which the Faith Foundation was established.

Scott Ellis, Treasurer: Scott Ellis serves as Treasurer and Board Chair of the Faith Foundation, providing financial oversight, strategic guidance, and leadership in support of the Foundation's mission to expand affordable housing opportunities and strengthen communities through faith-based service. Scott is the owner of E4 Roofing & Construction, a Georgetown, Texas-based company he has successfully led for more than 15 years. Through his business leadership, he has earned a reputation for integrity, accountability, and a commitment to serving customers with excellence. His experience as a business owner provides the Foundation with valuable financial, operational, project management, and organizational expertise. In addition to his business leadership, Scott brings practical construction and housing industry knowledge that directly supports the Foundation's mission. His experience in residential and commercial construction, project coordination, budgeting, contractor management, and building systems provides valuable insight as the Foundation develops affordable housing initiatives and evaluates housing-related opportunities. His understanding of construction costs, building practices, property improvement, and long-term asset stewardship helps ensure that projects are approached responsibly, efficiently, and with a focus on maximizing community impact. A longtime resident of Georgetown, Texas, Scott has called the community home for more than 24 years. He and his wife, Christy, have been married for 37 years and have raised two daughters together. Their enduring commitment to faith, family, and community reflects the values that guide both their personal and professional lives. Scott and Christy are active members of their local church, where they have dedicated themselves to serving others through ministry, fellowship, and community engagement. Scott is actively involved in Bible studies and men's groups, encouraging spiritual growth, mentorship, accountability, and Christian leadership. He has also participated in mission work in Mexico, demonstrating a servant's heart and a commitment to helping others beyond his local community. As Treasurer and Board Chair, Scott helps ensure that the Faith Foundation remains a faithful steward of its resources while advancing its vision of increasing access to affordable housing and creating opportunities for individuals and families to achieve long-term stability. His combination of business leadership, construction expertise, financial stewardship, and Christian service makes him a trusted leader and an invaluable member of the Foundation's governing team.

knowledgeBase.title: EXERCISE-HARNESS Mission Statement
knowledgeBase.content: We provide emergency and transitional housing support for families in rural Texas.

digitalTwins.mission: To help economically disadvantaged individuals achieve sustainable homeownership through down payment assistance vouchers, financial literacy education, and access to affordable modular housing.

programs.title: Down Payment Assistance Voucher Program
programs.description: The FAITH Foundation provides vouchers of up to 2500 dollars toward down payment costs on discounted modular housing units through partner Bright Box Homes. Program pathway: (1) Application and eligibility screening (2) Enrollment in mandatory Financial Literacy and Credit Repair Education Seminars (3) Matching with modular home inventory at discounted rates (4) Voucher issuance and closing assistance. Available homes include 20x20 and 20x40 expandable container homes, Apple cabins and space capsule units.

programs.title: Financial Literacy Education
programs.description: The FAITH Foundation provides financial literacy and credit repair education seminars covering budgeting, credit reports, credit repair strategies, mortgage preparation, loan terms, homeownership financial planning, and avoiding predatory lending. Completion is prerequisite for voucher issuance. Offered in-person and virtual.

programs.title: Land Acquisition and Site Development
programs.description: Long-term goals include acquiring land for modular home communities, site development with utilities and infrastructure, sourcing materials through grants and donations, overseeing construction of modular homes, and creating planned affordable communities. Vertically integrated model controls costs passing savings to homebuyers.

digitalTwins.mission: The FAITH Foundation exists to break the cycle of housing insecurity by providing financial education, homeownership instruction, and direct housing assistance to veterans, individuals experiencing homelessness, single parents, those in recovery, those reentering society, and other economically disadvantaged populations. Through our strategic partnership with Bright Box Homes, we transform charitable giving into permanent, affordable housing solutions

programs.title: Core Programs Overview
programs.description: Faith Foundation operates three interconnected housing programs across South Texas. The Down Payment Assistance Program provides direct financial awards to qualifying low-income individuals and families to secure permanent housing, targeting those who are employment-stable but lack savings for upfront housing costs. The Transitional Housing Program places individuals exiting homelessness, incarceration, or addiction treatment into stable transitional units with case management support, financial literacy training, and peer mentorship for up to 24 months. The Cornerstone Communities Initiative is the Foundation's flagship development program, acquiring land and deploying modular and manufactured housing units to create purpose-built micro-communities designed specifically for transitional residents. Each Cornerstone Community includes individual housing units, shared community spaces, and on-site access to case management and support services. As residents stabilize and transition to permanent housing, their units become available for new participants, creating a self-sustaining cycle of community impact. All programs prioritize military veterans, formerly incarcerated individuals reentering society, people in addiction recovery, single-parent families, and individuals experiencing or at risk of homelessness in rural and underserved South Texas communities.

opportunities.name: Rural Housing Preservation Grant
opportunities.description:
The Rural Housing Service (RHS) announces a notice in funding availability under its Housing Preservation Grant (HPG) program. The HPG program is a grant program which provides qualified public agencies, private nonprofit organizations, which may include but not be limited to, Faith-Based and Community Organizations, and other eligible entities grant funds to assist very low- and low-income homeowners in repairing and rehabilitating their homes in rural areas. In addition, the HPG program assists rental property owners and cooperative housing complexes in repairing and rehabilitating their units if they agree to make such units available to low- and very low-income persons. This action is taken to comply with Agency regulations found in 7 CFR part 1944, subpart N, which require the Agency to announce the opening and closing dates for receipt of preapplications for HPG funds from eligible applicants. The intended effect of this Notice is to provide eligible organizations notice of these dates.


$250,000 remains available from the American Relief Act, 2025 (Public Law 118-158) for Puerto Rico.


$2.09 million ($50,000 maximum award) is available for Calendar Year 2022 disaster assistance. The disaster funding is made available from the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023, Division N, Title I (Public Law 117-328). 2022 presidentially declared disaster areas can be viewed at https://www.fema.gov/disaster/declarations.

opportunities.name: Announcement of Stand Down Grants
opportunities.description:
The U.S. Department of Labor’s (DOL) Veterans’ Employment and Training Service (VETS) supports local Stand Down events that assist veterans experiencing homelessness by providing a wide range of employment, social, and health services.


Stand Down is a military term referring to an opportunity to achieve a brief respite from combat. Troops assemble in a base camp to receive new clothing, hot food, support services, and a relative degree of safety before returning to combat action. A DOL VETS-funded Stand Down event serves a similar purpose; however, it is intended for veterans experiencing or at-risk of homelessness. The critical services provided at these events are often the catalyst that enables those individuals to reenter the workforce.

 

VETS awards these noncompetitive grants on a first-come, first-served basis to support one-day or multi-day events at up to $7,000 or $10,000, respectively. They are collaborative events coordinated between VA, DOL, other federal, state, and local government agencies and community-based organizations providing services and supplies to veterans experiencing and at risk of homelessness. In the event of a federal disaster declaration, VETS will accept applications up to $50,000 to conduct Stand Down events in the impacted areas.


VETS awards Stand Down grants subject to the availability of federal funding. All costs incurred by the award recipient prior to the period of performance start date identified in the Notice of Award issued by the Department are incurred at the recipient’s own expense.
opportunities.eligibility_requirements:
See VPL 01-23 Section IV for the list of eligible applicants. Faith-based organizations are encouraged to apply, as are all organizations. Those that meet the eligibility requirements may receive awards under this announcement. DOL will not, in the selection of recipients and administration of the grant, discriminate on the basis of an organization’s religious character, affiliation, exercise, or lack thereof, or on the basis of conduct that would not be considered grounds to favor or disfavor a similarly situated secular organization.  State, Territory, and Possession, county, city, local, special district, and Native American tribal governments and agencies, non-profit and for-profit entities, state and local workforce boards, institutions of higher education, public and tribal housing authorities are eligible to apply.

Note: Organizations registered with the Internal Revenue Service as 501(c)(4) entities are ineligible to apply for this funding opportunity.

The purpose of the CEVSS Program is to encourage institutions of higher education (IHEs) to develop model programs to support veteran student success in postsecondary education by coordinating services to address the academic, financial, physical, and social needs of veteran students.
